About This Report

This report is an Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) report publicly disclosed by CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as "CSPC," "we," "the Group," or "the Company"). It aims to respond to stakeholder expectations and present the Company's philosophy, management approach, actions, and performance in environmental, social, corporate governance, and sustainable development.
Basis of Preparation

This report has been prepared in accordance with Appendix C2 "Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code" to the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on The Main Board of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)'s IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information and the IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures . It also references the GRI Sustainability Reporting Standards issued by the Global Sustainability Standards Board (GSSB), as well as major ESG rating indices in the capital markets such as the MSCI ESG Ratings.
Reporting Period and Frequency
This is an annual report for the year 2025, covering the period from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025. Certain content appropriately includes historical data for comparison purposes.
Reporting Scope

CSPC regularly reviews the reporting scope to ensure that this report covers all material issues that have a significant impact on the Group's overall business. Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) data presented in this report covers all production enterprises within the Group, while the policy descriptions and the reporting scope of other data are consistent with that of the Annual Report. Unless otherwise stated, social and governance data are consistent with the scope of the Company's consolidated financial statements.
Data Sources and Reliability

The data and case studies presented in this report are primarily derived from the Company's internal statistical reports and related policy documents. We are committed to ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the reported information and to avoiding any false or misleading statements. Unless otherwise stated, all monetary amounts in this report are expressed in Renminbi (RMB). This report is published in both Chinese and English. In the event of any discrepancies between the two versions, the Chinese version shall prevail.
Reporting Principles

Materiality: This report identifies key issues that need to be responded through stakeholder surveys and materiality analysis, and highlights the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues that may have a significant impact on investors and other stakeholders.

Quantitative: This report discloses key quantitative performance indicators, provides definitions of these indicators, and explains calculation methods and underlying assumptions. Detailed data and calculation methods can be found in the relevant sections of this report.
Balance: The contents of this report reflect the objective facts and disclose indicators that involve both positive and negative information.

Consistency: As the tenth ESG report issued by the Company, it maintains consistent disclosure practices. Reporting scopes and data collection tools have been standardized. Any changes in disclosure metrics are noted to facilitate an objective and accurate understanding of the Company's ESG performance by stakeholders.
Confirmation and Approval

The Board of Directors of the Company have reviewed and approved this report, ensuring that its content contains no false records, misleading statements, or major omissions. The Board also regularly monitored ESG matters and reviewed progress against relevant targets during the reporting period.
Report Access
This report is available for review and download on the websites of the Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited at www.hkexnews.hk and the Company's website at www.cspc.com.hk.
For further inquiries or any comments or suggestions regarding this report, please contact us via email at esg@cspc.hk or through the Company's website.
Chairman's Message

The year 2025 marks a pivotal year for CSPC as we advance high-quality development to greater depth. It is also an important year for deepening our sustainable development strategy and fully delivering on our corporate social responsibilities. In the face of rising global demand for healthcare and the fast-moving wave of industry transformation, CSPC has remained committed to its original mission of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," integrating ESG principles into every aspect of corporate development, demonstrating resilience amid challenges, and moving forward with resolve through change.
Innovation-driven growth builds new engines for development.

Innovation is embedded in CSPC's DNA and remains the core strength with which we respond to the demands of our time. Guided by our dual strategy of "innovation + internationalization," we continued to increase investment in R&D. In 2025, our R&D expenses reached RMB 5.809 billion, accounting for approximately 28.2% of revenue from finished drug business. The Group had more than 200 innovative drug and novel formulation projects under development. Supported by eight core technology platforms, including nanomedicine, ADC, and mRNA vaccines, we have not only further strengthened our presence in key therapeutic areas such as oncology, neurology and psychiatry, and cardiovascular diseases, but also continued to make progress in rare disease drug development. To date, 9 products have received orphan drug designation from the U.S. FDA, demonstrating through concrete action our contribution to the "Healthy China" initiative.

text: Quality first reinforces the foundation of responsibility.

Quality is the lifeline of an enterprise and our solemn commitment to hundreds of millions of patients. We have consistently upheld the quality policy of "ingenious manufacturing with craftsmanship and high quality," and established a quality management system covering the entire product life cycle to ensure that every tablet and every formulation can stand the test of quality. In 2025, we further strengthened end-to-end quality control from R&D to production. Multiple subsidiaries obtained ISO 9001 Quality Management System certification, all pharmaceutical production lines passed GMP certification, and we successfully passed 62 inspections by domestic and international drug regulatory authorities during the reporting period, safeguarding patients' health with outstanding quality.
local_heading: Quality first reinforces the foundation of responsibility.

text: Green Development paints a new ecological landscape.

Anchored in China's "dual carbon" strategy, CSPC has embedded green development into every stage of its operations. We have established comprehensive energy and environmental management systems. Seven subsidiaries passed ISO 50001 Energy Management System certification, 11 sites passed ISO 14001 Environmental Management System certification, and 5 production bases were recognized as national-level green factories. text: 2025, we continued to advance energy-saving and technological upgrade projects such as photovoltaic power generation and waste heat recovery. Green electricity consumption reached 177,823.51 MWh, while the compliant treatment rate of waste gas, wastewater, and waste remained at 100%. Through practical action, we are protecting the environment and contributing to the building of a beautiful China where humanity and nature coexist in harmony.
People-oriented development gathers strength for progress.

Talent is the Company's most valuable asset and the core engine of innovation-driven development. Upholding our talent philosophy of "valuing talent and capability, embracing diversity, and helping people succeed," we have built a career development system covering the entire employee life cycle. In 2025, women accounted for 48% of our workforce, while the proportion of women in the middle- and senior-management team rose to 59%, reflecting a stronger culture of diversity, equality, and inclusion. We also upheld the bottom line of workplace safety. Nine subsidiaries passed ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System certification, and throughout the year there were no work-related fatalities or confirmed occupational disease cases, ensuring every employee's peace of mind and dignity through comprehensive occupational health protection.
local_heading: People-oriented development gathers strength for progress.

text: Responsibility in action shows our support to society.

As a responsible corporate citizen, CSPC integrates social responsibility throughout its value chain. In 2025, in recognition of our sustained commitment and innovative practices in social responsibility, we were selected for the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce's "2025 Outstanding Cases of Social Responsibility of Chinese Private Enterprises." We continued to advance inclusive healthcare. Three patient assistance programs have cumulatively benefited more than 100,000 patients. Through a public welfare model that encourages participation by all employees, we continue to deliver warmth and demonstrate responsibility.

Looking ahead, CSPC will continue to take technological innovation as its driving force and responsibility as its foundation, working hand in hand with partners across the value chain and all sectors of society. Through high-quality development, we will contribute to common prosperity and bring even greater "CSPC strength" to the building of a healthy China and the advancement of Chinese modernization.

text: Board ESG Statement

CSPC fully recognizes the significant impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues on corporate sustainability, stakeholder trust, and long-term value creation. In accordance with the Code of Corporate Governance for Listed Companies issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the relevant requirements of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited, the Company has progressively integrated ESG concepts and standards into its corporate governance and business management systems.

The Company has established a sound ESG governance framework, forming a three-tier management structure comprising the "Board of Directors - ESG Professional Guidance Team - ESG Working Group," which provides organizational support for the orderly advancement of ESG management. As the highest decision-making body and governing body for ESG matters, the Board of Directors leads and assumes overall responsibility for the Company's environmental, social and governance work. Its main responsibilities include formulating ESG strategies and targets, reviewing assessments of material risks and opportunities, overseeing the response to and management of ESG-related risks and opportunities with a material impact on the Company's business, and reviewing ESG-specific policies and the ESG report. As the core management body for ESG work, Professional Guidance Team is responsible for assessing ESG-related risks and opportunities, coordinating resource allocation, reviewing ESG management matters and policies, and supervising the timely alignment of the Company's ESG policies with national requirements. The ESG Coordination Office serves as the executive body for ESG matters, coordinating and advancing the implementation of ESG-related work across departments. In addition, the Company has established an ESG Working Group and subsidiary-level ESG Working Groups, which are responsible for implementing annual ESG work plans, participating in the formulation of ESG targets and the preparation of the ESG report, and collaboratively advancing specific ESG initiatives.

The Board places great importance on the identification and determination of material ESG topics. In 2025, based on the two dimensions of "impact materiality" and "financial materiality," the Company systematically reviewed and dynamically refined its double materiality topics in accordance with the process of "identification - research assessment - confirmation." The 2025 double materiality matrix was updated and disclosed upon review by the Board.

This report provides a detailed account of the progress and implementation of the Company's ESG management in 2025. Following review by the Professional Guidance Team, it was submitted to the Board of Directors for consideration and approval on 25 March 2026.
Company Profile

Guided by the philosophy of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited has grown through innovation into an international and innovation-driven enterprise with a workforce of 20,000 employees. The Company (Stock code: 01093.HK) was listed on the Main Board of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited in 1994 and was included as a constituent of the Hang Seng Index in 2018. It also ranked 19th globally among Citeline published pharmaceutical companies by R&D pipeline size, representing China's pharmaceutical industry on the global stage and serving patients worldwide.

Through innovation on a global scale, we continuously deliver better healthcare solutions for humanity. With five major global R&D centers and a high-caliber R&D team of more than 2,000 professionals, we are advancing research into new technologies, new targets, and new frontiers, with a focus on key treatment areas including oncology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, gastrointestinal and metabolic, and anti-infectives. We have established a diversified product portfolio spanning three major business segments: finished drugs, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and functional foods. Supported by eight technology platforms, including nanomedicine, mRNA, and ADC, CSPC is focused on six core therapeutic areas: oncology, neurology and psychiatry, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, metabolism, and anti-infectives. The Group currently has more than 200 innovative drug candidates in development, including over 90 macromolecular drugs, more than 60 small molecule drugs, and over 50 novel formulations.

ESG Governance Structure

The Group has established a three-tier ESG governance structure comprising the governance level, management level, and execution level to advance sustainable development. With clearly defined roles and responsibilities and implementation at each level, this structure ensures that ESG management is fully embedded in the Group's operations and long-term development.
Table: CSPC ESG Governance Structure
Board of Directors
Management Level
ESG Committee
Execution Level
ESG Working Group

The Board of Directors is the highest decision-making body and governing body for the Group's ESG work. It leads and assumes responsibility for the Group's ESG governance matters, and oversees and reviews the Group's ESG-related development strategies, targets, plans, and other matters that may have a material impact on the Group. It serves as the governing body responsible for addressing ESG issues such as climate change, occupational health and safety, business ethics, and information security, and performs the following duties: (1) Establishing the Group's ESG organizational structure; (2) Overseeing the Group's ESG management and practices; (3) Approving the Group's ESG strategy, targets, and development plans.

The Group has established an ESG Committee as the core management body for ESG work. It consists of 3 to 4 directors of the Group and the head of the ESG Working Group, and is responsible for assisting in the formulation of ESG strategic targets and implementation plans, as well as reviewing and evaluating the achievement of ESG targets by each business division. The main responsibilities of the ESG Committee include:
Assisting in the formulation of the Group's ESG strategy and targets, and in implementing related measures and action plans;
Executing decisions related to ESG targets;
Reviewing the specific ESG indicators and targets of each business division and functional department;
(4) Evaluating and assessing the execution and progress of ESG work across business divisions and functional departments.

The Group has established an ESG Working Group responsible for the specific implementation and execution of ESG work. The main responsibilities of CSPC's ESG Working Group include: (1) Implementing the Group's ESG work requirements;
Reporting work progress to the ESG management level;
Taking the lead in organizing the preparation of the ESG report and management systems; (4) Collecting information related to the Group's ESG indicators;

(5) Benchmarking against industry standards and making recommendations to improve ESG ratings; (6) Organizing ESG-related training and coordinating resources across the Group; During the year, CSPC identified a total of 18 topics. Among them, climate change response and carbon emissions, product safety and quality, product innovation and R&D, and access to healthcare are classified as high-priority topics under both dimensions.
Formulating the Group's annual ESG policies, targets, and assessment measures.

We have incorporated ESG performance into the evaluation of senior management, assessing performance comprehensively across three dimensions: business performance, capability assessment, and values alignment. The evaluation results are directly linked to key decisions including performance bonuses, adjustments to grade-based compensation, promotions, talent activation, and training and development.
Double Materiality Assessment

To further enhance ESG management performance and disclosure transparency, the Group conducted an ESG double materiality assessment. Taking into account industry characteristics, the current state of our business, regulatory trends, and the core concerns of stakeholders, we carried out a comprehensive evaluation of relevant topics from the two dimensions of "impact materiality" and "financial materiality." The assessment results were reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors, based on which the materiality matrix for the year was finalized and established, providing a sound basis for the focused execution and effective implementation of our ESG strategy.
Table: Double Materiality Assessment Process

Background Analysis and Preliminary Topic Identification | • Analyze the Group's business model, operational characteristics, industry environment, and major stakeholder groups to define the background and boundaries of the assessment.
Establishment of the Preliminary Topic List | • Integrate industry benchmarking, regulatory guidance, international standards, and the Group's own operational realities to screen, consolidate, and refine topics, forming a comprehensive preliminary pool of topics.
Double Materiality Assessment | • Impact Materiality Assessment: The Group evaluates the impact materiality of each topic across three dimensions. The first is likelihood of risk exposure, namely the probability that the topic may have a negative impact on the Group. The second is severity, referring to the potential extent of damage if the impact occurs. The third is risk adaptation capacity, meaning the effectiveness of the Group's existing control systems in responding to the risk. Based on the analysis of these dimensions, a conclusion is reached regarding the impact materiality of each topic. • Financial Materiality Assessment: We adopted an expert assessment approach and organized the heads of the Finance Department and other relevant departments to evaluate the potential multi-dimensional impacts of each ESG topic on the Group's revenue, costs, assets, and valuation. We also analyzed the pathways and potential scale of these impacts on the Group's financial performance over the short, medium, and long term. Based on this multi-stage assessment, each topic was assigned an overall financial materiality score, and the final rating was determined according to pre-set thresholds.
Integrated Analysis and Topic Confirmation | • Integrate the results of the impact materiality and financial materiality assessments to identify the double materiality topics that are of major significance to the Group's sustainable development.
Review, Reporting and Disclosure | • The assessment process, methodology, and materiality matrix are submitted to the Board for review and confirmation before public disclosure.

CSPC is committed to building a professional corporate governance system to ensure transparency and effectiveness in decision-making. By strengthening our risk management framework, upholding business ethics and an anti-corruption stance, and fostering a culture of compliance across the organization, we support the Group's steady and sustainable development.
1.1 Corporate Governance

Sound corporate governance is a core pillar and fundamental safeguard for CSPC's steady development. The Group continues to optimize its governance structure and enhance governance effectiveness in all respects, ensuring compliant and efficient operations and laying a solid foundation for long-term sustainable development.
1.1.1 Corporate Governance Structure

CSPC complies with the Main Board Listing Rules of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited, and other applicable laws and regulations. We continue to improve our management systems and have established a governance framework that is well-structured, clearly accountable, and highly efficient in operation, thereby continuously advancing the modernization of the Group's governance capabilities.

As the Group's decision-making body, the Board of Directors is responsible for setting strategic directions, establishing objectives and business plans, and overseeing financial and operational performance. The Board performs its duties in strict accordance with the Group's governance requirements, and the procedures for convening, holding, and voting at Board meetings are all in compliance with relevant regulations. The Board has established 3 specialized committees under its authority: the Remuneration Committee, the Nomination Committee, and the Audit Committee. Each committee performs its duties in strict accordance with applicable requirements, providing strong support for the professionalism and efficiency of the Board's deliberations and decision-making. In 2025, the Group had a total of 17 directors, and Board attendance reached 100%.

Remuneration Committee

1.1.2 Board Composition

Board independence and diversity are core safeguards for CSPC's sustainable development. As of the end of the reporting period, the Board comprised 17 directors, including 6 independent non-executive directors and 1 female director. Independent directors accounted for approximately 35.30% of the Board, while female directors represented 5.9%.

The Group regards the independent non-executive director system as a core component of a sound corporate governance framework. In managing board independence, the Group applies strict standards and requires independent non-executive directors to maintain an independent position and provide objective views in performing their oversight duties. In the selection and appointment process, the Group places particular emphasis on reviewing the independence of candidates' identities and relationships to ensure that independent non-executive directors can effectively perform their duties, enhancing the Board's supervisory effectiveness and decision-making quality and improving the fairness and transparency of corporate governance.

The Group also strives to promote diversity on the Board in areas such as gender, culture, and professional expertise, in order to align with the Group's business needs. In the nomination process, factors such as age, gender, cultural background, and ability to collaborate are considered comprehensively, with a view to creating long-term value for the Group and its stakeholders. Members of the Board bring extensive professional backgrounds and industry experience spanning corporate governance, financial management, risk management, human resources management, and market development in the energy sector. During the reporting period, the Group had 16 directors with pharmaceutical industry backgrounds and 3 directors on the Audit Committee with relevant industry experience.

section: 1.2.1 Risk Management / Board Diversity Composition of CSPC
text: The Group has established a full-cycle risk management approach and incorporated ESG risks into its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) system. We have improved the entire risk management process, covering risk identification, risk assessment, risk response, issue resolution, review and reflection, as well as follow-up control and monitoring, thereby forming a closed-loop risk management framework. We adopt a three lines of defense mechanism for compliance risk prevention and control, comprising "functional departments (business, operations, and marketing) - compliance management department - security audit department," to ensure that risk management is effectively implemented across all aspects of the Company's operations, helping the business reduce operational risks and better respond to changes in the external environment.

text: 1.2.2 Compliance Management

The Group strictly complies with applicable laws, regulations, and government regulatory requirements, and incorporates compliance requirements into its policies and procedures while continuously strengthening compliance management under the foundational framework CSPC Compliance Management System. We have further refined a comprehensive compliance management framework covering compliance objectives, system development, operating mechanisms, compliance culture, supervision and accountability, and continuous improvement, thereby comprehensively enhancing our level of lawful and compliant operations.

To further strengthen the Group's overall governance standards, we have established a Compliance Committee, composed of the Group CEO and the presidents of each business division, as the highest decision-making body responsible for overseeing compliance matters across the Group. Under the Compliance Committee, the Compliance Department is responsible for coordinating and advancing the implementation of compliance work, while providing comprehensive compliance guidance and professional support to business divisions and relevant functional departments.
Compliance Audits

The Group regularly conducts internal and external compliance audits to monitor the actual implementation of compliance work across departments and to provide a comprehensive view of the current state of compliance management. In accordance with the CSPC Internal Audit Procedures, the Group carries out its work independently under the guidance of the Board's Audit Committee. We have established an audit framework, carried out various forms of audit oversight, promoted rectification and accountability, and pursued claims recovery and loss mitigation, with coverage spanning financial, management, engineering, fraud, and special audits, all aimed at improving the internal control system and preventing operational risks. In 2025, the Group's internal audit work was grounded in further strengthening the institutional framework. Leveraging big data analytics to optimize risk assessment, we carried out systematic audits focusing on core processes such as sales and collections, procurement and payments, and production and warehousing, identifying control deficiencies and making recommendations for improvement. Through closed-loop follow-up on rectification, accountability, and loss recovery, we continuously enhanced the effectiveness of internal controls and the soundness of operations.
Compliance Training

The Group continuously improves employees' compliance awareness and execution capabilities through regular compliance training programs covering all employees, while also providing targeted training for key personnel to ensure the effective operation and rigorous oversight of the compliance management system. In doing so, we foster a corporate culture in which compliance principles are deeply embedded, while firmly upholding the Company's compliance bottom line.

section: Anti-Corruption Management of Suppliers / 1.3 Integrity and Compliance

section: Anti-Corruption Management of Suppliers / 1.3 Integrity and Compliance
text: CSPC strictly complies with the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the Interim Provisions on Prohibiting Commercial Bribery, and other applicable laws and regulations. We have revised internal policies applicable to all employees and all suppliers of the Group, including the Employee Code of Integrity and Conduct, the Gifts and Monetary Gifts Management System, the Business Hospitality Management Measures, the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, and the Tender Supervision and Management System. We have also newly formulated the Anti-Corruption and Commercial Bribery Policy of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Limited. These efforts continuously strengthen our business ethics management mechanisms, regulate employees' conduct in integrity-related matters, and ensure that business ethics work is governed by clear rules and standards. During the reporting period, the Group was not involved in any litigation related to corruption, nor did it incur any financial losses arising from corruption-related incidents.

section: Anti-Corruption Management of Suppliers / 1.3 Integrity and Compliance
text: We have established and continuously improved a comprehensive business ethics management system. We formulated the Employee Code of Integrity and Conduct, which clearly defines the responsibilities of all levels, including the Board of Directors, in business ethics management, building a business ethics governance structure led by the Board of Directors, with dedicated supervision functions responsible for the overall development of integrityrelated systems and frameworks. Presidents and general managers of subsidiaries and business divisions serve as the primary persons responsible for integrity and self-discipline at work, while middle- and senior-management personnel in subsidiaries and business divisions serve as professional leads, supported by designated supervisors. Managers at all levels assume corresponding management and leadership responsibilities within their respective scopes, ensuring that oversight responsibilities are carried out professionally and effectively across the organization.

section: Anti-Corruption Management of Suppliers / 1.3 Integrity and Compliance
text: Anti-Corruption Management of Suppliers

section: Anti-Corruption Management of Suppliers / 1.3 Integrity and Compliance
text: To regulate supplier conduct and foster a clean business environment, the Group has established the Tender Supervision and Management System and the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, requiring suppliers to sign the Sunshine Cooperation Agreement before participating in tendering activities. Integrity clauses are also incorporated into standard contracts to give such requirements legal effect. At the same time, through a full-process supplier management system, we continuously assess suppliers' business ethics performance during cooperation and blacklist suppliers that violate relevant requirements, thereby safeguarding fairness in the tendering process and the integrity and compliance of supplier relationships. In 2025, the Group carried out audits covering the full supplier lifecycle, including supplier onboarding, tendering and bidding, contract signing, payment, and acceptance and warehousing, and organized the signing of 10,254 Sunshine Cooperation Agreements, covering all suppliers participating in the Group's tendering and negotiation processes.

In addition, we carry out at least 1 business ethics audit each quarter covering high-risk areas such as tendering and procurement, sales expenses, and supplier management, while also using big data analytics to support risk assessment. During the reporting period, we carried out 26 audit projects across the Group, mainly covering professional areas such as sales, engineering, procurement, and production.

During the reporting period, we further deepened our training model of "full coverage + focus on key personnel," providing foundational red-line education to all employees while delivering targeted and in-depth training for personnel in key positions. text: On 25 December 2025, the Group organized a featured in-person activity, an integrity-themed sand table simulation under its Integrity Awareness Month program, titled "The Road of Choice". Through an innovative and immersive format, the activity delivered a practical lesson in ethical conduct and integrity at work. By simulating real business scenarios, participants were guided through group discussions and strategic decision-making exercises, helping them gain a deeper understanding of the importance of integrity boundaries and the serious consequences of misconduct and legal violations. A total of 150 employee representatives from key positions across various departments and subsidiaries took part in the activity.

section: 1.3.2 Building a Culture of Integrity / 1.3.3 Anti-Unfair Competition
text: CSPC actively participates in establishing and maintaining a fair and orderly market environment, and works to prevent and combat monopolistic conduct, abuse of market dominance, and improper concentration of undertakings. The Group strictly complies with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, the Anti-monopoly Guidelines in the Field of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients , and other applicable laws and regulations. On this basis, we have established internal management policies such as the Dishonest Blacklist Management System, which clearly defines 15 categories of unfair competition conduct. Where a business partner is found, upon investigation, to have engaged in non-compliant conduct, the Group will disclose the matter internally in accordance with its policies and place the party on the dishonest blacklist. From the effective date of such blacklisting, the partner will be prohibited from participating in any tendering projects of the Group, and all direct and indirect business dealings with the Group will be fully terminated. In 2025, the Group was not involved in any litigation or material administrative penalties arising from unfair competition conduct.

section: 1.3.2 Building a Culture of Integrity / 1.3.3 Anti-Unfair Competition
text: In addition, to ensure that all business activities are conducted in a fair, impartial, straightforward, and transparent environment, we require the relevant business department to arrange for counterparties to sign the Sunshine Cooperation Agreement before entering into any formal agreement or launching any tendering process. The agreement clearly defines specific forms of unfair competition and dishonest conduct, with the aim of establishing safeguards at the outset of the business relationship and effectively preventing and curbing unfair competition.

text: CSPC places great importance on the development of business ethics oversight and whistleblowing mechanisms. In strict accordance with applicable national laws and regulations, we have established a comprehensive whistleblower protection framework and formulated, and continue to improve, internal policies such as the Whistleblower Protection and Reward Policy. These policies systematically regulate reporting channels, handling procedures, and graded reward mechanisms based on the level of contribution, ensuring that all complaints and reports are responded to and handled in a timely and effective manner.

section: 1.3.2 Building a Culture of Integrity / 1.3.3 Anti-Unfair Competition
text: The Group fully respects whistleblowers' wish to report anonymously and strictly fulfills its responsibilities for whistleblower protection. We keep strictly confidential all information relating to whistleblowers, including their names, employers, addresses, and the content of their reports, in order to safeguard their safety. In the process of receiving reports and complaints or conducting verification work, we do not disclose whistleblowers' identities. Any act of retaliation discovered will be dealt with seriously in accordance with applicable rules and laws.

Quality Management System

CSPC strictly complies with a wide range of national laws and regulations, including the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Administrative Measures for Drug Registration, the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Drug Production , the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, the Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs, the Pharmacovigilance Quality Management Standards, the Good Laboratory Practice for Non-clinical Laboratory Studies, the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Drug Distribution and Use, the Measures for the Administration of Drug Recalls, and the Provisions on the Supervision and Administration of Drug Marketing Authorization Holders in Fulfilling Their Primary Responsibility for Drug Quality and Safety . Based on these requirements, we have established a prevention-oriented, comprehensively controlled quality management and full-process traceability system to ensure quality management throughout the entire life cycle of pharmaceuticals.

The Group rigorously fulfills its primary responsibility for drug quality and safety by formulating and implementing the Quality Responsibility Management System , under which the safety responsibilities of drug marketing authorization holders and food manufacturers and operators are clearly embedded across all management dimensions. Through a cross-functional quality coordination mechanism, we have established a matrix of responsibilities and accountabilities covering the full product life cycle and the entire value chain, ensuring that quality responsibilities at every stage are performed with precision. In addition, the Group relies on a four-level quality assurance system comprising the Group, company, department, and team levels. Supported by a professional quality management team and refined vertical management, this system enables comprehensive and in-depth oversight of quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) across the Group's member enterprises.

Quality Audits

The Group has established a quality audit mechanism and regularly conducts both internal and external audits. Issues identified are subject to follow-up, rectification, and verification, enabling the continuous enhancement of quality management standards.
· Internal Audits

CSPC continues to supervise, inspect, and guide its subsidiaries through a normalized internal audit mechanism. In 2025, the Group formed dedicated inspection teams by selecting professional inspectors from its internal inspector pool to carry out in-depth quality system inspections and special crosschecks among subsidiaries. During the year, a total of 37 system, unannounced, and special inspections were completed. Through these internal audits, communication and the sharing of advanced quality management practices and typical issues identified in both internal and external inspections were further strengthened across subsidiaries.
· External Audits

The Group actively aligns itself with major global regulatory standards and continues to validate the compliance and internationalization of its quality system through external audits and authoritative certifications. All subsidiaries operate in strict accordance with China's GMP requirements and continue to improve production quality management with international standards as the benchmark. As of the end of the reporting period, the Group held a cumulative total of 15 CEP certificates, 15 ANDA products, and 1 NDA product. Relevant active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and formulation enterprises manage their quality systems in accordance with ICH Q7, U.S. cGMP, and EU GMP requirements. All pharmaceutical production lines of the Group have passed GMP certification. During the reporting period, the Group underwent 62 inspections by domestic and international drug regulatory authorities, all of which were successfully passed.
Key Quality Certification Achievements in 2025

Formulation Companies: In 2025, the Group's formulation companies underwent a total of 41 inspections by domestic drug regulatory authorities, 1 EU GMP inspection, 1 FDA inspection, and 5 inspections by overseas regulatory authorities, all of which were successfully passed. In total, the formulation companies passed 48 inspections by domestic and international drug regulatory authorities during the year.

API Companies: In 2025, the Group's API companies underwent a total of 11 inspections by domestic drug regulatory authorities, 1 German GMP inspection, 1 FDA inspection, and 1 EU certification inspection, all of which were successfully passed.

text: Quality Management for Preclinical Drug Research

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: At the preclinical research stage, the Group strictly follows standards and regulatory requirements including the Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs, Good Manufacturing Practice for Drugs - Investigational Products for Clinical Trials, the Administrative Measures for Drug Registration, and the Chinese Pharmacopoeia, while also incorporating its own R&D practices to establish and continuously improve the quality management system for preclinical pharmaceutical research.
local_heading: Quality Management for Preclinical Drug Research

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: The Group's quality management system for preclinical pharmaceutical research deeply integrates foundational management with risk management, with the aim of ensuring the steady advancement of pharmaceutical R&D. On the foundational management side, we have established a multi-dimensional management framework covering quality, materials, equipment, and laboratory management. Through refined control over pilot production, analytical method development, reference standards management, and electronic data management, together with risk control measures for deviations and changes, we have enabled effective integration between pharmaceutical R&D and subsequent manufacturing. On the risk management side, we have adopted the ICH Q10 quality risk management concept, covering the full lifecycle from drug development to pre-launch. By identifying and assessing compliance risks at critical research stages, and through closed-loop management of deviations and quality feedback, we ensure that risks are effectively controlled before project submission. Since 2018, the Group has undergone on-site inspections for pharmaceutical development for a cumulative total of 16 projects, all of which were successfully passed, including 2 FDA registration inspection projects, 4 inspections by the National Medical Products Administration, and 10 inspections by provincial drug regulatory authorities. Looking ahead, we will continue to deepen both foundational and risk management and further enhance the effectiveness of our R&D quality system.

text: Clinical Research Quality Management

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: In accordance with internationally recognized ICH guidelines and the relevant requirements of the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), the Group has established and continues to refine a Clinical Quality Management System (cQMS) covering the entire clinical trial process. In 2025, guided by the core principle that "quality built by design, and responsibility runs throughout the process," the Company worked to elevate quality management from a single focus on compliance inspection to a strategic capability that drives R&D efficiency and sustainable development, building a dynamic management system covering the full value chain and highly responsive to regulatory trends. During the year, the Group continued to optimize and improve its policies and procedures, revising and refining more than 20 SOPs, work manuals, and templates to ensure that the quality management system remained closely aligned with the latest domestic and international regulations, including ICH GCP E6 (R3), as well as the Group's own organizational structure.

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: The Group implements a front-loaded risk management approach, moving the starting point of quality management significantly forward to the clinical trial project initiation and protocol design stages. Potential risks are assessed based on multiple dimensions, including historical audit data, site qualifications, researcher experience, and national inspection findings. Through the establishment of a clinical key document review mechanism and the strengthening of upfront resource allocation, systemic risks are mitigated at the source. The Group adopts a combined management model of routine monitoring and risk-based oversight, using centralized statistical monitoring to capture abnormal signals in key indicators such as enrollment pace, data query rates, and protocol deviations in real time. This enables monitoring and quality control resources to focus on the most critical data and processes, ensuring the compliance of trial conduct and the authenticity of results.

section: Table: Certification and GMP Compliance of Formulation Companies / Certification Status
text: In addition, the Group places strong emphasis on knowledge management and continuous improvement. By systematically analyzing deviations identified in projects, their root causes, and corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), we continuously improve the Company's knowledge base and risk database. In 2025, we conducted annual training covering all clinical R&D personnel, including more than 50 specialized skill enhancement sessions. We also shared best practices through weekly themed capability-building activities, fostering a culture in which all employees participate in quality management. Looking ahead, we will actively explore the application of artificial intelligence in risk identification and data verification, driving the system toward greater intelligence and agility. By upholding the highest quality standards in innovative drug development, we aim to protect patient rights and interests and further strengthen the foundation for the Company's sustainable development.
2.1.3 Manufacturing Quality Management

CSPC is committed to integrating technological innovation with institutional development, deeply combining advanced manufacturing equipment with intelligent information systems to build a high-quality manufacturing system covering the entire value chain from materials and production to product release.

All subsidiaries of the Group have established comprehensive quality management systems covering six core systems of pharmaceutical manufacturing and operations. Each subsidiary has also put in place mechanisms for tracking laws, regulations, and standards, enabling the timely follow-up of the latest compliance requirements issued both domestically and internationally, and their accurate translation into internal management systems. This ensures both the regulatory compliance of the quality management system and its effective guidance for manufacturing activities. At the same time, through the establishment of quality risk management systems, the Group and its subsidiaries use scientific risk assessment tools to identify potential risks affecting product safety and quality controllability from multiple dimensions and formulate control plans accordingly, with the goal of providing patients with high-quality, safe, and controllable products.
Product Manufacturing Quality Control

With the SAP system as the main backbone, supplemented by multiple specialized management systems, the Group comprehensively supports smart manufacturing through digitalization. Each company has established full-process management systems covering material receipt, production control, finished product release, and distribution. Combined with the application of information systems, this has enabled effective full life-cycle product management and continuous improvement. On the hardware side, production workshops are designed and constructed in strict accordance with the standards of smart manufacturing and internationalization, reaching internationally leading levels. Through the SAP system upgrade project, the Group conducted an in-depth review of the entire business workflow of its manufacturing centers, from sales planning, production planning, and procurement demand to production task execution, and carried out end-to-end standardization and integration of the functions and processes of surrounding systems such as MES, WMS, LIMS, and APS. On this basis, the Group successfully shifted from a make-to-stock model to an "order-based management" logic, significantly improving management efficiency.

The application of advanced production equipment and information tools such as MES, WMS, LIMS, and traceability systems provides the core driving force for the Group's smart manufacturing. In terms of software management, subsidiaries across the Group have established rigorous production and process control systems and operating procedures aimed at standardizing employee operations, effectively preventing mix-ups and errors, and minimizing the risks of contamination and cross-contamination. After receiving materials, production workshops carry out manufacturing strictly in accordance with process requirements and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for each position. Once finished product sampling is completed, products are transferred to the warehouse pending inspection and are subject to strict control by the quality management department. The QC laboratories fully apply the LIMS system for automated data management, effectively reducing human error. In addition, critical production areas' pressure differentials and temperature/humidity levels, warehouse temperature and humidity, laboratory refrigerator temperatures, and stability chamber temperature and humidity are all equipped with automatic monitoring and alarm systems. Through an early warning mechanism triggered whenever parameters exceed limits, delays caused by human judgment are reduced. Each batch of product is assigned a unique batch number, ensuring a full-process and traceable quality closed loop throughout the product life cycle.
Intelligent management system: SAP system as the main line, supplemented by professional management system
Case Study: Ouyi "5G Workshop"

The Group's Ouyi "5G Workshop" was included in the 2024 national list of 5G factories. Through an efficient, stable, and secure hyper-converged server architecture and a fully connected 5G network framework, the project has enabled the secure operation and interconnectivity of all systems. Driven by data, the workshop has achieved full-process control in areas such as precise material pull, secure weighing control, real-time data transmission, and authentic record storage, ensuring transparency and traceability throughout the product life cycle.
Materials Management

The Group implements rigorous supplier and material admission systems. By centrally managing a shared supplier roster and applying unified on-site audit standards, the Group has achieved centralized control at the source of the supply chain. Each company has established a Supplier Management System to regulate the full lifecycle of supplier admission, evaluation, and phase-out.

In the material flow process, the Group strictly implements the Material Receipt, Storage, and Issuance Management System, ensuring that all materials are procured only from qualified suppliers and stored separately in strict accordance with storage requirements. Through clear signs of pending inspection, released, and non-conforming materials, together with physical segregation measures, the risk of errors is effectively prevented. All materials must be inspected by the quality management department and approved for release before they enter the production process.
Finished Product Release

The Group strictly implements the release responsibility system for Marketing Authorization Holders (MAH). Where contract manufacturing is involved, the contracting party and the contract manufacturer clarify their respective quality responsibilities in production and release by signing manufacturing agreements and quality agreements. After each batch has completed testing against the established standards, it must undergo final review by the Qualified Person (QP) authorized by the drug marketing authorization holder, ensuring that only products meeting quality standards are released to the market.

2.1.4 Quality and Safety Management

CSPC is committed to providing society with products of high quality, strong efficacy, and proven safety and reliability. Guided by the principle that "quality is built by design," we apply risk management tools to quality management throughout the entire product life cycle, from R&D to commercial sales. At the same time, the Group has established a sound market surveillance mechanism. Each subsidiary has implemented systems for customer complaint management, return management, product recall management, and corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), which are used to collect and analyze market feedback and formulate continuous improvement measures.
Quality Risk Management

The Group's philosophy on quality risk management is "prevention first, combination of prevention and control, and dynamic management." In accordance with the relevant requirements of ICH Q9 on quality risk management, we have established a sound risk control framework and a Quality Risk Management System to comprehensively identify risk points that may affect product quality throughout the product life cycle. During the risk assessment process, the quality management department organizes expert teams to use professional assessment tools such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), factor analysis, and fishbone diagrams to assess risks across different products and processes, and implements graded management based on the results.

The Company has also enhanced inventory security for major products and strengthened the reliability and safety of supply by implementing dual sourcing arrangements and multi-line production. At present, the vast majority of raw materials are covered by dual sourcing arrangements, and major products are supported by multiple production lines operating in coordination.
Table: Quality Risk Management Philosophy

Prevention First | Identify quality risks in advance, conduct assessment and management updates; Classify risks by materiality, formulate control plans early, and adopt various early warning and response measures.
Combination of Prevention and Control | Combine prevention and control by not only preventing risk events in advance, but also actively controlling risks once they arise.
Dynamic Management | Ensure rapid adaptation of risk prevention and control to changes in the external environment, and revise and improve the system in a timely manner in response to changes in national laws and regulations, reforms in management systems, improvements in management standards, and evolving business management needs.

text: Leveraging its comprehensive quality risk prevention and control system, the Group has clearly established an assessment process for quality and safety risks. Full-process management is implemented from risk assessment, risk control, and risk review, with risk communication and risk management tools embedded throughout the process.
Pharmaceutical Quality and Safety Traceability

Leveraging its information systems, the Group has established a traceability system covering the entire life cycle of pharmaceuticals, enabling full-process tracking from material receipt and product release to commercial distribution. In addition, all formulation manufacturing companies have established comprehensive pharmacovigilance systems and adverse drug reaction reporting and monitoring systems to safeguard patient medication safety on all fronts.
Operation of the Pharmacovigilance System

The Group has dedicated pre-marketing and post-marketing pharmacovigilance teams and has built a pharmacovigilance system covering the entire product life cycle, while overseeing the effective operation of the system across all formulation companies. The Group has established a Drug Safety Committee responsible for handling major drug safety incidents at the Group level, while each formulation company is responsible for executing its company-level system and has clearly defined and continuously improved the processes for collecting, reporting, and handling adverse drug reactions. Each member enterprise is equipped with dedicated personnel commensurate with its production scale to ensure the effective implementation of management systems.

In terms of system standardization, in accordance with the requirements of the Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GVP), the Administrative Measures for Adverse Drug Reaction Reporting and Monitoring, and other relevant regulations, the Group has established 87 management procedures, policies, and guidance documents. These include the Pharmacovigilance Management System, Emergency Response Plan for Major Adverse Drug Reaction Events, Drug Safety Committee Management System, Internal Audit Management System for the Pharmacovigilance System, Pharmacovigilance Database Management System, and Standard Operating Procedures for Drug Safety Information Collection. Of these, 53 documents were developed by the pre-marketing pharmacovigilance team and 34 by the post-marketing pharmacovigilance team, covering key areas such as individual case safety report handling, literature searches, Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs), Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRERs), signal detection, and risk management.

The Group has developed a comprehensive pharmacovigilance plan and implements continuous monitoring measures. In terms of system operation, the Group has established a multi-channel information collection network. Dedicated personnel conduct real-time monitoring and collection through channels including the national direct adverse reaction reporting system, dedicated email addresses, clinical studies, market programs, academic literature, and relevant websites and forums. Supported by its pharmacovigilance information system, the Group processes, evaluates, and reports individual suspected adverse reaction cases to ensure that, in the event of cluster or major adverse reaction incidents, emergency measures can be launched promptly and relevant national and local regulatory authorities can be notified in a timely manner. In addition, each formulation company under the Group submits its annual pharmacovigilance report and periodic drug safety reports on schedule every year, using data-driven approaches to strengthen safety management and fully protect patient medication safety. In 2025, the Group did not receive any reports of cluster adverse reaction incidents caused by product defects.

In line with its pharmacovigilance quality objectives, the Group regularly conducts internal pharmacovigilance quality audits to review relevant policies, procedures, and their implementation, thereby managing the quality of the pharmacovigilance system and its activities. Through the continuous refinement and optimization of the pharmacovigilance system and its operation, the Group continues to enhance pharmacovigilance within its full life-cycle quality management framework. In 2025, CSPC successfully passed multiple regulatory inspections.

To strengthen pharmacovigilance capabilities, the Group adopts a multi-dimensional training model combining internal and external resources. Internal training, delivered through centralized sessions and online learning, systematically enhances risk awareness among all employees and strengthens the professional capabilities of dedicated personnel. External training connects closely with professional courses offered by national and provincial monitoring institutions and advanced research institutes, enabling the Group to stay abreast of domestic and international developments and risk management practices and thereby drive the continuous innovation of its pharmacovigilance system.
Product Recalls

To address the recall of defective products, each subsidiary of the Group has formulated and implemented a Product Recall Management System, clearly defining the respective responsibilities of relevant departments such as quality and sales, and establishing standardized product recall procedures. In strict accordance with the severity of potential drug safety risks, the Group classifies recalls into Class I, Class II, and Class III to ensure a precise risk response. At the same time, the quality management departments of each company regularly organize mock recall drills to continuously verify and ensure the effective operation of the recall system. In 2025, no recalls were recorded for any products sold or delivered by the Group due to safety or health reasons.
Counterfeit Drugs and Infringement Management

The Group has established a Quality Information Management System, which sets out the procedures for handling information related to counterfeit drugs and infringement. A dedicated rights protection task force has been set up to define follow-up actions, as well as the responsibilities and division of work among departments, based on the level of impact and urgency of counterfeit or infringement cases. Where necessary, the Legal Affairs Center and the Patent and Government Affairs Department will initiate relevant legal proceedings. The rights protection task force follows up on the progress of each case until it has been fully resolved. Within one week after the conclusion of each case, a summary report is prepared, and corresponding follow-up preventive measures are formulated to standardize handling procedures and prevent similar issues from recurring. Where counterfeit or infringement incidents give rise to reputational risks, they are handled in accordance with the General Rules for Media Crisis Emergency Response of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group.

section: 2.1.5 Building a Quality Culture / Case Study: 2025 Quality Month Activities
text: CSPC is an innovation-driven pharmaceutical enterprise integrating R&D, manufacturing, and sales, and is one of the leading players in China's pharmaceutical industry. Upholding our corporate mission of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," we actively pursue innovation to address unmet clinical needs and provide patients with innovative treatment solutions.

section: 2.1.5 Building a Quality Culture / Case Study: 2025 Quality Month Activities
text: 2.2.1 R&D Layout

section: 2.1.5 Building a Quality Culture / Case Study: 2025 Quality Month Activities
text: The Group consistently adheres to its FIRST R&D philosophy: Focus, Innovation, Responsibility, Synergy, and Top-notch. With innovation and internationalization as the dual drivers at the core of its R&D and innovation strategy, the Group is accelerating its transformation from a leader in generic drugs into a company centered on "global innovative drugs + high-end formulations," with the goal of becoming an innovative pharmaceutical enterprise with international influence. The Company focuses on six major therapeutic areas: oncology, anti-infectives, immunology and respiratory, neurology and psychiatry, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular, and gastrointestinal and metabolic diseases. Supported by eight core technology platforms, including nanomedicine, antibodies/fusion proteins, ADC, small molecules, siRNA, mRNA, cell therapy, and long-acting injectables, the Group has built an R&D system with three major pillars: macromolecular drugs, small molecule drugs, and novel formulations.
2.2.1.1 R&D Management System

The Group has established an R&D management system under the overall coordination of the R&D and Innovation Committee. Under this structure, dedicated divisions for preclinical research, clinical research, U.S. R&D, and global clinical development enable specialized management across the entire R&D process. At the same time, the Group has developed an institutional framework covering funding, project management, talent, and compliance. Through policies such as the Financial Management and Assessment System for the R&D System, the R&D Project Initiation Management System, and the Measures for the Recommendation and Management of Outstanding Talent, we standardize expense management and scientific decision-making to support the sustainable development of R&D. To further strengthen talent incentives, the Group conducted a talent review and salary and promotion adjustments for all R&D personnel in 2025.

The Group has built a high-caliber international R&D team of more than 2,000 professionals and established five major global innovation R&D centers, continuously exploring new technologies, new targets, and new fields. In 2025, the Group's R&D investment reached RMB 5.809 billion.
2.2.1.2 R&D Platform Development

The Group has developed eight core technology platforms, namely nanomedicine, antibodies/fusion proteins, ADC, small molecules, siRNA, mRNA, cell therapy, and long-acting injectables, and has established a full R&D value chain from the laboratory to commercial production.
Table: Eight Core Technology Platforms

Technology Platform | Technological Advantages and R&D Achievements
Nanomedicine Platform | As the world's largest nanomedicine R&D and industrialization base, we have successfully commercialized 8 products, including Mitoxantrone Hydrochloride Liposome and Paclitaxel (Albumin-bound).
ADC Platform | We have developed proprietary site-specific conjugation technology. Nectin4-ADC, Claudin18.2-ADC, and ROR1-ADC have already been out-licensed overseas, and 10 products have entered or are about to enter the clinical stage.
Antibody / Fusion Protein Platform | 5 products, including Narlumosbart Injection and Enlansobart Injection, have been approved for marketing. A further 30 monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, and antibody fusion proteins are under development.
mRNA Vaccine Platform | We have systematically addressed key challenges in LNP delivery and industrialization, and successfully developed and launched China's first COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. Vaccines for RSV, HPV, and VZV have entered the clinical research stage.
siRNA Platform | We have laid out more than 10 pipeline projects targeting various chronic diseases, among which siRNA projects including PCSK9, Lp(a), ANGPTL3, and C5 have successfully entered the clinical research stage.
Small Molecule Platform | We use AI-based drug screening technology to improve efficiency. More than 20 projects are under development. Prusogliptin tablets, a Class 1 innovative chemical drug, were approved for marketing in January 2025, and strategic collaborations have been established with AstraZeneca and others.

text: 2.2.1.3 R&D Achievements

CSPC focuses on six major therapeutic areas: oncology, anti-infectives, neurology, cardiovascular, immunology and respiratory, and gastrointestinal and metabolic. The Group currently has more than 200 innovative drug and novel formulation projects under development. The commercialized products on the market comprehensively cover all six of these major therapeutic areas.
· New drug approvals

In 2025, a total of 4 new products were approved for marketing, and 9 generic drugs received marketing approvals. Among them, Prusogliptin tablets (DPP-4 inhibitor), a Class 1 innovative chemical drug provided a better glucoselowering option for patients with type 2 diabetes, while Meloxicam Injection (III), a nanomedicine product, offered a fast-acting and safe treatment option for acute moderate to severe pain management.
· Clinical trial approvals obtained

In 2025, the Group obtained 40 clinical trial approvals for first indications, including 26 approvals from the NMPA and 14 from the FDA, as well as 27 clinical trial approvals for additional indications, all from the NMPA. Representative approved projects included SYH2059, SYS6045 (HER2-ADC), and SYS6017 (mRNA vaccine), demonstrating the Group's strong clinical translation capabilities.
· Innovative drug and novel formulation pipeline

Currently, the Group has over 200 innovative drugs and formulations in its R&D pipeline, including more than 90 large molecules, over 60 small molecules, and over 50 novel formulations. There are over 160 ongoing clinical trials, many of which feature products with broad market prospects that demonstrate significant advantages over existing therapies in terms of efficacy and safety.

text: · Antimicrobial Resistance

section: Table: Awards and Honors in 2025 / September 2025
text: The Group is fully aware that antimicrobial resistance has become a serious threat to global human health and regards it as a major public health risk issue. To effectively address this challenge, the Group takes proactive action in innovative drug R&D by continuously advancing the research and development of novel antibacterial drugs and anti-resistance-related projects through both in-house R&D and external technology collaboration, with the aim of reducing the risk of antimicrobial resistance at the source and overcoming resistance challenges through innovation.

section: Table: Awards and Honors in 2025 / September 2025
text: In terms of clinical application and life-cycle management, the Group places strong emphasis on the rational use of antibiotics. We strictly comply with national regulations and clinical guidelines, including the Administrative Measures for the Clinical Use of Antibacterial Drug s and the Notice on Further Strengthening Antimicrobial Drug Management to Curb Resistance , and strengthen prescription drug management in a comprehensive manner in conjunction with the graded management catalogues issued by provinces and municipalities. The Group actively supports medical institutions in implementing the grading management of antibacterial drugs and physician prescribing authority management. In addition to providing professional guidance on dosage and preparation methods, we proactively provide healthcare professionals with training on antimicrobial resistance control and the optimization of treatment regimens for drug-resistant infections through academic annual meetings and other forums across various fields. Furthermore, leveraging our comprehensive pharmacovigilance plan, the Group monitors safety data in real time, updates product instructions in a timely manner, and continues to provide scientific medication consultation services to the public and healthcare professionals. Through these combined efforts, we seek to improve the clinical use of antibacterial drugs and comprehensively curb antibiotic misuse.

text: The Group places great emphasis on the skill empowerment and capability development of its research personnel and has established a regular internal and external training mechanism. In 2025, the Group organized one to two technical training sessions per month for all R&D personnel, covering core areas such as drug registration regulations, interpretation of regulatory guidelines, process development, and quality control.

section: 2.2.1.4 R&D Training / 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management
text: For clinical researchers, the Group conducted 103 R&D capability enhancement training sessions over the course of the year, including internal project experience-sharing sessions and a range of external professional courses, such as Training on Common Methods for Tumor Molecular Pathology Diagnosis and the DIA Capability Development Academy Course on Pharmacovigilance and Risk Management. This training series was aimed primarily at juniorand mid-level employees. Through an average of four to five internal and external sharing sessions per month, it continuously strengthened the team's professional breadth and practical capabilities.

section: 2.2.1.4 R&D Training / 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management
text: 2.2.2 Intellectual Property and Patent Protection

section: 2.2.1.4 R&D Training / 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management
text: Intellectual property is a core strategic resource of the enterprise and an important indicator of overall corporate strength and core competitiveness. The Group strictly complies with intellectual property laws and regulations in China and other jurisdictions, including the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the Enterprise Intellectual Property Management Specification, the Patent Cooperation Treaty, and the Paris Convention. Within this legal framework, the Group actively develops its patent portfolio and protects R&D innovation. The Group has established a dedicated department for intellectual property management and, leveraging its own R&D resource advantages, continues to refine a pharmaceutical R&D system that integrates generic and innovative development, with the goal of using its intellectual property strategy to drive high-quality corporate growth.

section: 2.2.1.4 R&D Training / 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management
text: 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management

section: 2.2.1.4 R&D Training / 2.2.2.1 Intellectual Property Protection and Risk Management
text: Guided by the management policy of "encouraging innovation, controlling risks, effectively utilizing intellectual property, and enhancing the Group's core competitiveness and strategic advantage in IP," the Group has established a patent protection system suited to its operations and new-drug R&D activities. We protect core R&D achievements from multiple angles and in a comprehensive manner, and we have formulated robust patent filing, protection, and risk-avoidance strategies for key products. In generic drug development, the Group flexibly uses patent design-around strategies, patent challenges, and patent licensing to address market-launch compliance issues. The Group has also established a full-cycle patent early-warning analysis and risk-control mechanism covering the entire period from project initiation to product launch. It conducts regular diagnostic analyses so that, while avoiding infringement risks, it can also make appropriate use of legal means to safeguard the Group's lawful rights and interests. In 2025, the Group obtained recertification of its intellectual property management system and has now successfully passed seven on-site certification audits in total.

text: 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: CSPC regards "participants' rights first, ethics before science" as an unwavering core principle in clinical R&D, making it explicit that under all circumstances, the protection of participants' dignity, safety, rights, and well-being takes precedence over scientific exploration and social benefit. Every clinical study we conduct strictly follows international and domestic ethical and quality standards, including but not limited to the World Medical Association Declaration of Helsinki, ICH GCP, the Good Clinical Practice for Pharmaceutical Products (GCP 2020), the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the Vaccine Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Measures for the Administration of Drug Registration. Meanwhile, the Group fulfills its corporate responsibilities by strictly implementing the requirements on ethical submission and reporting set out in ICH GCP E6(R3), the CIOMS Guidelines, and the Measures for the Ethical Review of Life Science and Medical Research Involving Humans, ensuring that research is conducted within a compliant, scientific, and ethical framework.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: 2.2.3.1 Ethics Governance and Informed Consent

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: The Group's ethics governance covers the full life cycle of clinical research, including study design, execution, oversight, and closeout. At the protocol design stage, we communicate with ethics committees in advance and solicit views on key ethical issues so that study protocols better reflect best ethical principles. Before any study begins, it must be reviewed and approved by an independent ethics committee (IEC/IRB), and participants' right to be informed is fully protected throughout implementation. We explain the study objectives, methods, possible risks, and potential benefits to participants in detail, ensuring that they voluntarily sign informed consent forms on the basis of a full understanding of the relevant information. If protocol amendments occur during the study, or if any new information arises that could affect a participant's decision to continue, the Group promptly reports the matter to the ethics committee and communicates it to participants simultaneously, ensuring that they remain fully informed on an ongoing basis.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: 2.2.3.2 Ethical Reporting, Oversight, and Data Compliance

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: Throughout the clinical research process, the Group strictly complies with domestic and international requirements for ethical submissions and reporting. All study data are collected, managed, and analyzed within a stringent oversight framework to ensure authenticity and reliability while fully protecting participant privacy. All of our clinical studies are registered concurrently on ClinicalTrials.gov or the Drug Clinical Trial Registration and Information Disclosure Platform of China. After study completion, results are published through authoritative domestic and international journals, academic conferences, and other channels to enhance the transparency of clinical research. In addition, the Group has an independent quality assurance department responsible for maintaining the clinical quality management system (cQMS) and auditing trial quality, ensuring through rigorous internal audits that ethical standards are effectively implemented.
