section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: The Group consistently places participant safety and rights at the center of every stage of clinical research and embeds this requirement into the work of every clinical staff member. We require employees to keep strictly confidential any trial participant privacy or sensitive information they encounter in the course of their work and to prevent any leakage of information. To address possible risks and unexpected situations, the Group purchases adequate insurance for every clinical trial to ensure full protection of trail participants' rights and interests. We regard the protection of participants' safety and well-being as the lifeline of our corporate social responsibility and, by building a sound safety assurance mechanism, ensure that the entire clinical research process remains safe and ethical.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: 2.2.4 Animal Protection

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: CSPC upholds the principle of harmony between humans and nature and is committed to the scientific, reasonable, and humane use of laboratory animals. We strictly comply with national and local laws and regulations, including the National Standards for the Environment and Facilities for Laboratory Animals of the People's Republic of China, the Guidelines for the Ethical Review of Laboratory Animal Welfare of the People's Republic of China, the Measures for the Administration of Laboratory Animals of Hebei Province , and the Regulations on the Administration of Laboratory Animals, to ensure that animal experiments are lawful and compliant.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: The Group has established a Laboratory Animal Welfare Ethics Committee and has formulated and implemented systems such as the Provisions on the Ethical Welfare Management of Laboratory Animals and the Standard Operating Procedures for Ethical Review of Laboratory Animals . We have built a professional breeding and husbandry management system and a veterinary health care team to ensure that laboratory animals enjoy their basic rights, including freedom from hunger and thirst, comfort, freedom from pain, injury, and disease, freedom from fear, and the freedom to express natural behaviors. All animal laboratories under the Group have obtained Laboratory Animal Use Licenses and successfully pass annual license inspections and special animal welfare reviews each year.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: In practice, the Group has deeply embedded the widely recognized "3R Principles" (Replace, Reduce, and Refine) into its management system. In routine research, we improve the comfort of laboratory animals by optimizing experimental design and installing advanced sanitary facilities, while reducing animal use to the extent possible without compromising scientific validity. Meanwhile, in supplier cooperation, we explicitly require suppliers to comply with standards related to laboratory animal protection.

section: 2.2.3.3 Protection of Clinical Trial Participants' Safety and Rights / 2.2.3 Clinical Ethics
text: To ensure that all personnel, including part-time staff and contractors, understand their ethical and legal responsibilities related to welfare, we regularly conduct internal technical compliance training and external professional skills training. During the reporting period, the Group recorded no misconduct related to animal welfare and no penalties resulting from non-compliance in animal experimentation.
2.3 Quality Services

CSPC consistently adheres to "customer first" as a core behavioral principle and is committed to building a high-quality service system covering the entire product life cycle. By establishing in-depth customer communication mechanisms, we convert market demand into momentum for management improvement and, while ensuring high-quality service, we strictly safeguard customer information security and protect customer rights and interests in all respects.
2.3.1 Customer Service System

The Group has established a dedicated customer service department within the marketing decision-making center to systematically classify customer needs and effectively translate them into R&D directions, key technical requirements, and service improvement targets, ensuring implementation throughout the full process from R&D, procurement, and production to sales. In 2025, in response to customer feedback on logistics improvements, the Group optimized targeted services by improving bidding procedures, raising admission standards, and strengthening process oversight.
2.3.2 Customer Satisfaction and Communication Mechanisms

Through regular client satisfaction surveys and quality management reviews, we assess the soundness of complaint investigation procedures and capture changes in market demand in real time. During the 2025 Quality Month, the Group collected 245 customer satisfaction questionnaires, and the results showed both product satisfaction and service satisfaction at 98.8%. Through ongoing analysis of feedback and root-cause tracing, the Group continues to improve its operating performance and ensure that service quality consistently exceeds customer expectations.
2.3.3 Customer Complaint Mechanism

The Group has established a sound Client Complaint Management System and effective communication and feedback mechanisms. To ensure that client needs are effectively addressed throughout R&D, procurement, production, and sales, we systematically classify the information collected and accurately translate it into R&D directions, key technical requirements, and service improvement targets. Each member enterprise conducts regular annual quality management reviews to scientifically evaluate the scope and procedures of complaint investigations and continuously optimize improvements in conjunction with client satisfaction surveys. To strengthen market product quality monitoring, business personnel proactively conduct frontline visits and sampling, using dual quality confirmation through both retained company samples and marketed products to ensure the safety and robustness of products placed on the market.

In terms of complaint handling effectiveness, the Group has established strict tiered response standards and conducts annual summaries and evaluations of quality complaints. In 2025, the Company received a total of 172 complaints, of which the quality complaint rate was 0.18%. All complaints were closed out strictly in accordance with the applicable requirements, and both the complaint handling rate and complaint resolution rate reached 100%.

2.3.4 Responsible Marketing

CSPC places great importance on compliant operations and has officially released its Responsible Marketing Policy, which explicitly prohibits false advertising, concealment of information, and unfair competition. To ensure the effective implementation of this policy, the Group provides dedicated responsible marketing training to all employees (including full-time, part-time, and outsourced personnel), embedding compliance principles deeply into daily business activities. In addition, the Group has established a rigorous supervision and accountability framework. Led by the Supervision and Audit Department together with the Sales Committee, special audits and compliance assessments of marketing activities and policy implementation are conducted regularly across the Group. These efforts are supported by well-developed multi-channel whistleblowing mechanisms and a zero-tolerance accountability approach, ensuring tangible protection of customers' legitimate rights and interests and promoting fair market competition.

text: CSPC continues to deepen its centralized group procurement and control model. While ensuring supply stability and efficiency, it deeply integrates sustainability dimensions such as environmental protection, labor rights, and business ethics into supplier life-cycle management. By strengthening risk early-warning mechanisms, driving digital transformation, and promoting the development of a green industrial chain, we aim to work with global partners to build a resilient, green, and transparent sustainable supply chain ecosystem.

section: 2.3.5 Privacy Protection and Information Security / 2.4 Supply Management
text: The Group has formulated institutional documents such as the Supplier Management System and the Materials Procurement Management System. Under the overall coordination of the Group's centralized procurement center, key aspects including supplier admission, classification, evaluation, auditing, quality control, risk management, and integrity management are managed, and the supplier life-cycle management system is continuously improved. In 2025, the Group systematically optimized its management systems around supplier quality control, collaborative auditing, ESG management, and other areas, while continuing to enhance supply chain transparency and resilience through the electronic procurement platform (SRM). The Group also dynamically updated its supplier comparison survey form to further increase the weighting of price advantage, supply capability, and quality and R&D capability, while reducing the influence of scale-related factors.

section: 2.3.5 Privacy Protection and Information Security / 2.4 Supply Management
text: At the admission stage, the Group implements strict qualification review and compliance control, conducting comprehensive assessments of suppliers covering qualifications, product quality, supply capability, and social responsibility. On the premise of meeting quality standards, enhancing supply assurance, and maintaining price advantages, the Group gives priority to suppliers with stronger ESG performance.

section: 2.3.5 Privacy Protection and Information Security / 2.4 Supply Management

Based on performance, quality records, and compliance status, underperforming suppliers are simultaneously phased out so as to maintain healthy competition and continuous optimization in the supply structure.

text: 2.4.1.3 Supplier Evaluation

The Group has formed a supplier evaluation team composed of the quality management department, user departments, and the procurement department. Each year, the team conducts comprehensive evaluations and scoring of suppliers based on price, operating performance, financial condition, contract fulfillment capability, and ESG performance. Evaluation results are classified as excellent, good, qualified, or unqualified.
Classification Management and Audit Requirements

Implement tiered management for materials, utilizing methods such as on-site audits, questionnaires, or video audits accordingly. The audit cycle is 2 years in principle, which may be extended based on material quality reviews and supplier reputation assessments, but shall not exceed 5 years. The core objective of the audit is to verify qualification certificates and inspection conditions, as well as to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the production quality management system.
Incentive mechanism

Suppliers with excellent annual evaluation results and significant support for the Group may receive incentives such as priority procurement and increased delivery allocation. Suppliers rated as qualified but ranking relatively low may have their procurement share adjusted based on category and competitive conditions.
Rectification mechanism

Suppliers rated as unqualified are required to rectify within a specified period or will have their qualification revoked. Suppliers that engage in improper conduct, such as refusing to sign a contract after confirming a negotiated price on site, may be suspended from quotation for six months based on business needs; in serious cases, they may be eliminated or blacklisted.
In 2025, the Group completed audits of 728 suppliers, including 279 on-site audits and 449 document-based audits, achieving a 100% completion rate of annual supplier audit plan.
2.4.1.4 Supplier Risk Management

The Group conducts systematic risk identification at the admission stage, focusing on financial stability, production and supply capability, quality and process standards, and industry reputation. The Group has formulated the Supplier Management Policy, which stipulates that, in principle, the number of suppliers for raw and auxiliary materials shall be limited to two to three in order to ensure supply stability. In the event that there is only a single supplier, the Group will initiate the onboarding process for an additional supplier in accordance with the Change Management Policy and the Supplier Management Policy, carry out the corresponding quality studies, and, after completing the required filing procedures with the drug regulatory authorities in compliance with applicable regulations, include the supplier in the list of qualified suppliers, thereby eliminating the risks associated with reliance on a single supplier.

To ensure continuity of supply, the Group has implemented the Procurement Emergency Response Plan Management System, which clearly defines responsibilities, information reporting requirements, and response measures for various emergency events. In response to factors such as climate, policy, quality, EHS, logistics, and funding, the Group adopts multi-level management, information sharing, and business continuity planning measures. The Group regularly provides emergency response plan training to procurement personnel and reinforces implementation through reward and penalty rules.
2.4.1.5 Supplier Empowerment

The Group regularly conducts audits and exchanges with key suppliers on quality and supply chain stability. During on-site audits, it also provides concurrent training to suppliers covering the latest industry quality standards, environmental regulations, and related ESG core topics, thereby strengthening suppliers' capabilities in accident prevention and traceability.
2.4.2 Supplier ESG Management

CSPC is committed to building a sustainable supply chain, deeply embedding ESG factors into supplier life-cycle management and working to create a green, clean, and socially responsible supplier ecosystem.
2.4.2.1 Supplier ESG Screening Standards

At the supplier admission stage, the Group promotes the ESG concept and, while ensuring quality standards, supply assurance, and price competitiveness, treats ESG performance as a core weighting factor in supplier screening.
Admission evaluation

The Group gives priority to suppliers that have passed assessments relating to the environment, labor, ethics, carbon emissions, and similar factors, and that meet the Group's environmental protection and safety management requirements. All new suppliers must sign a Quality Assurance Agreement and commit to cooperating with the Group's integrity-building efforts.
· Qualification requirements

At the supplier onboarding stage, the Group actively recommends that suppliers provide supporting documents meeting green procurement control requirements. We encourage suppliers to obtain certifications such as ISO 14001 Environmental Management System certification and ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System certification, and we treat certification status and social responsibility performance as preferred factors in supplier selection.
Supplier Management System Certification Status
Number of suppliers certified to ISO 14001 Environmental Management System Number of suppliers certified to ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System
2.4.2.2 Green Supply Chain Management System

In accordance with standards including GB/T 39257-2020 Evaluation Specification for Green Supply Chain Management of Green Manufacturing Enterprises and GB/T 43902-2024 Implementation Guidelines for Green Supply Chain Management of Green Manufacturing Enterprises, the Group has established and implemented the Green Supply Chain Management Operating Procedures. It integrates product life-cycle and circular economy concepts throughout the entire chain, from supplier admission to waste recycling. Meanwhile, the Group has built a green supply chain management system that centrally stores product environmental data, test reports, and supplier performance evaluations. Through homepage announcements and publication of institutional documents, green information is made visible and traceable throughout the chain.

Led by the Group's centralized procurement center and supported by a dedicated task force composed of procurement, EHS, and quality departments, the Group regularly convenes green supply chain promotion meetings to ensure that ESG assessment is deeply embedded in the supplier evaluation system.
Carbon footprint monitoring

The Group proactively collects data from major material suppliers on carbon reduction plans, energy-saving and consumption-reduction projects, and Scope 1, 2, and 3 carbon footprint figures. For partners demonstrating significant emissions reduction results, the Group appropriately increases their delivery allocation under equivalent conditions, thereby encouraging collaborative decarbonization across the supply chain.
· Categorized management and prioritization

In line with the Group's overall ESG strategy, the centralized procurement center ranks suppliers according to Scope 3 carbon emissions and gives priority to ESG-focused governance for suppliers of key fossil energy and non-renewable resources, helping ensure the steady achievement of the Group's overall carbon neutrality goals.

text: Adhering to the core philosophy of "All for Good Medicine, All for Mankind's Health," CSPC practices the concept of "Green Development for a Better Life." It integrates environmental protection into its development strategy and continuously optimizes its environmental management system through green manufacturing, energy conservation and emissions reduction, and cleaner production. The Group actively implements green engineering and smart upgrading projects, significantly improves resource utilization efficiency, reduces carbon emissions, and is committed to building an environmentally friendly pharmaceutical enterprise.
local_heading: Rooted in Green Safeguarding the Future 03

text: 3.1 Climate Change Response

CSPC actively implements the national "dual carbon" strategy and empowers the transformation and upgrading of the pharmaceutical industry through a green and low-carbon development pathway. The Company continues to enhance its climate resilience, improve its climate governance structure, systematically identify climate-related risks and opportunities and formulate response strategies, and advance the smart and green transformation of its production system, thereby building an environmentally friendly pharmaceutical industry ecosystem.
3.1.1 Governance

CSPC has built a three-tier climate governance structure under which the Board of Directors makes strategic decisions, the ESG Working Group provides overall management and coordination, and each subsidiary is responsible for concrete implementation, thereby systematically advancing the achievement of climate goals. Each year, when reviewing the progress of annual ESG management work and the ESG report, the Board systematically reviews the management progress of climate-related issues.

At the same time, the Company regularly organizes specialized training for the Board and key departments across subsidiaries to continuously enhance awareness of climate-related risks, opportunities, and international frameworks at all levels, thereby systematically strengthening strategic decision-making and execution capabilities in climate governance.

text: Climate Resilience Assessment 5

To verify the adaptability of the Group's existing business strategy under different climate futures, the Group conducted in-depth physical-risk climate scenario analyses for its major operating locations across China, including Hebei, Heilongjiang, Inner Mongolia, Guangdong, and Jiangsu, and simultaneously performed qualitative stress testing for transition risks.
Physical-risk Resilience

For physical risks, the Group used the SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios published by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and carried out scenario analysis based on the geographic locations of its principal assets. The main findings are as follows:
· Extreme precipitation

Operating sites in Taizhou, and Guangzhou face relatively high extreme-precipitation risk across all scenarios and time horizons. Sites in Yuncheng and Shijiazhuang face comparatively lower risk under SSP1-2.6, but the risk rises to a relatively high level under SSP5-8.5.
· Typhoons

Coastal and near-coastal operating sites in Yantai, Taizhou, and Guangzhou continue to face relatively high typhoon risk across all scenarios and time horizons, while inland and northern locations remain at relatively low risk.
· Extreme cold

Operating sites in Harbin and Hohhot face relatively high extreme-cold risk across all scenarios and time horizons, whereas other locations face lower risk. The assessment also indicates that under SSP5-8.5, the frequency and intensity of extreme-cold events decline across the Group's operating locations.
Extreme heat

The Guangzhou operating site faces the most severe extreme-heat risk. Sites in Shijiazhuang, Xingtai, Yuncheng, Jiujiang, and Xuancheng also face significant challenges from extreme heat. The assessment shows that under the medium- and long-term SSP5-8.5 scenario, the frequency and intensity of extreme-heat events in these regions will rise further, imposing higher requirements on plant temperature control and cold-chain logistics.
Water scarcity

Operating sites in Hohhot, Yuncheng, Yantai, and Taizhou face pronounced water-scarcity risk under all scenarios, while Shijiazhuang also face considerable water stress. Northern China and certain coastal areas may experience increasingly persistent water constraints over the long term.

Through scenario analysis of physical risks, we have clearly identified material climate-risk exposures in each region, which supports more forward-looking preparedness. Within the scope of our assessment, we believe the Group overall has relatively strong climate resilience. Under the selected scenarios and time horizons, the physical climate risks identified above are not expected to have a material adverse impact on the Group's overall business continuity or core financial position. Benefiting from the Group's diversified production layout, adequate safetystock management, and continually improving business continuity plans, we are able to flexibly allocate resources during extreme-weather events. Going forward, we will continue to monitor high-risk regions and adopt further response measures where necessary.
Transition Risk and Opportunity Resilience

For transition risks, the Group referenced the International Energy Agency (IEA) Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS) and Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario (NZE), and conducted climate-resilience stress testing across its core businesses and full value chain over the short, medium, and long term.

The assessment shows that under the STEPS scenario, current climate policies advance broadly as expected, resulting in relatively moderate increases in compliance and operating costs that remain manageable within normal operations. Under the stricter NZE scenario, characterized by aggressive decarbonization, carbon-pricing mechanisms spread rapidly worldwide, and the Group may face rising carbon-compliance costs in the medium and long term. Meanwhile, upstream suppliers, such as those providing chemical raw materials and packaging materials, may pass through carbon costs, increasing the Group's procurement prices.

Although the Group is not currently included in a mandatory carbon emissions trading market and has not yet experienced a material financial impact from transition risks, there remains substantial uncertainty over the medium to long term regarding whether it may be brought into scope, as well as the timing of policy implementation and future carbon-pricing levels. Under such an aggressive scenario, the Group may not only face a direct rise in its own carbon-compliance costs, but also an upward shift in its overall procurement cost base as upstream suppliers in high-carbon sectors pass their carbon costs downstream.

In response to policy uncertainty over the medium and long term, the Group is moving proactively rather than reactively, steadily advancing decarbonization across the value chain while actively seizing opportunities created by the transition to a low-carbon economy. The Group expects to continue energy-efficiency upgrades at production sites and explore the use of renewable energy and environmentally friendly packaging, thereby effectively hedging long-term risks of rising energy and compliance costs while enhancing overall supply-chain resilience.
Financial Impact

During the reporting period, climate-related risks did not have a significant adverse impact on the Group's working capital, carrying value of assets, or overall profitability. All impacts remained within the controllable range of routine operating budgets. The Group does not currently identify any material risk in the next reporting year that is expected to cause a significant adjustment to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities.

Guided by a Prevention Foremost strategy, the Group proactively incurred targeted capital expenditures and operating expenditures during the current period to strengthen climate resilience and steadily advance the low-carbon transition. During the reporting period, more than RMB 30 million was invested in energy-efficiency retrofits and the introduction of new high-efficiency energy-saving equipment; in addition, more than RMB 1 million was invested in water-saving and water-recycling projects.

3.1.3 Risk Management

The Group has established a closed-loop management process of "identification-assessment-response-monitoring and reporting," integrating the identification, response, and monitoring of climate-related risks and opportunities into the Company's overall risk management system to enhance adaptability and response capability in relation to climate change.
Risk Assessment

Monitoring and Reporting Identify potential uncertainties arising from climate-related transition risks and physical risks across business processes. Through scenario analysis, stakeholder interviews, industry benchmarking, policy tracking, and data screening, develop a preliminary list of climate-related risks and opportunities.
Conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis of identified risks.

Risk analysis: The Group assesses each risk's potential impact on finance, operations, and strategy, together with likelihood and time horizon, and uses scenario analysis to quantify potential financial impacts.

Risk evaluation: The Group classifies and prioritizes risks based on established criteria, forming a company-level conclusion on climate-change risks and clarifying the key risk areas requiring priority attention and their pathways of impact on the business.
Based on the priorities resulting from the risk assessment, formulate and implement response measures.

Strategy implementation and execution: Within the framework of the Company's overall risk management and business strategy, business and functional departments develop specific action plans, allocate resources, and execute them.

Integration and optimization: Climate-risk response measures are integrated into existing risk management processes, investment decisions, operational management, and financial planning to ensure effectiveness and strengthen business resilience.
Establish an ongoing closed-loop management mechanism to ensure the effectiveness and adaptability of risk-management activities.

Monitoring: The Group establishes Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and performance indicators to regularly monitor changes in the status of identified risks, as well as the implementation progress and effectiveness of response measures.
Review and Update: The Group regularly reviews and optimizes the overall climate risk management process, risk assessment results, and response strategies, or when significant changes occur.

Internal and External Reporting: The Group regularly reports to the board of directors on the status of climate risk management, material risk exposures, and response effectiveness. We also disclose information on governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets externally in accordance with frameworks such as the TCFD recommendations.
3.1.4 Metrics and Targets

CSPC focuses on improving energy efficiency in production and optimizing its energy mix to systematically reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Through green process upgrades, clean-energy substitution, and intelligent energyefficiency management, the Group continues to reduce GHG emissions intensity per unit of output and has established a value-chain-wide emissions monitoring and evaluation mechanism to support phased reduction targets.
Greenhouse gas reduction target of CSPC:
By 2030, the Group aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions per unit of revenue by 50% relative to 2017, the baseline year.

text: 3.2 Environmental Management

CSPC regards environmental protection as a core component of high-quality corporate development. The Group continues to deepen the development of its environmental management system, improve management mechanisms and processes, advance green transformation in a practical manner, and actively contribute to ecological and environmental protection.
3.2.1 Environmental Management System

The Group strictly complies with environmental laws and regulations such as the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Pollutant Discharge Permit Regulation, and the Energy Conservation Law of the People's Republic of China. It has formulated internal management systems including the Environmental Protection Responsibility System, Environmental Management Manual, and Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Policy, and established a top-down environmental management structure that clearly defines the environmental responsibilities of each department and assigns accountability level by level, ensuring orderly and effective implementation of environmental protection work and providing strong support for a green, low-carbon, and environmentally friendly operating system. As of the end of the reporting period, the Group had not incurred any major environmental penalties.

In addition, in line with internal systems such as the CSPC EHS Assessment, Rewards and Penalties System and the CSPC EHS Incident/Event Reporting, Investigation and Handling Management System, the Group evaluates employees on environmental performance. Environmental indicators such as administrative penalties for safety and environmental matters, negative media exposure related to safety and environment, pollutant leaks, chemical management, and pollutant-discharge control targets form an important part of ESG performance and are incorporated into the performance appraisal system for employees and senior management. Failure to meet the relevant targets directly affects performance results and may reduce compensation, ensuring full implementation of environmental responsibilities. Meanwhile, the Group has established a positive incentive mechanism to recognize and reward individuals and teams who demonstrate outstanding performance in EHS work.

text: CSPC continues to strengthen the development of its environmental management system. In accordance with the requirements of the ISO 14001 environmental management system standard, it dynamically tracks and evaluates performance against environmental indicators, driving environmental management toward greater standardization and systematization. By 2025, 11 sites of the Group had obtained ISO 14001 certification, providing strong support for the Group's green, low-carbon, and sustainable development.

In addition, the Group has established a comprehensive environmental impact compliance audit mechanism and regularly conducts both internal and external audits of its environmental management systems in accordance with unified requirements, culminating in the preparation of detailed internal audit reports. During the reporting period, 11 sites completed internal environmental management system audits.

CSPC actively responds to the national call for green development and continues to advance green-factory construction. At present, the Group has 5 national-level green factories, 2 provincial-level green factories, and 2 municipal-level green factories. These factories widely apply advanced environmental technologies and high-efficiency equipment, significantly improving energy and resource utilization efficiency while promoting cleaner production and the adoption of low-carbon technologies, thereby supporting the Group's green transformation and building benchmarks for environmentally friendly, resource-efficient, and well-governed green manufacturing.
Case Study: Zhongnuo Recognized as a Municipal Green Factory

Zhongnuo was recognized as a "Municipal Green Factory," demonstrating its strength in green manufacturing. The Company follows a cradle-tocradle philosophy throughout the full product life cycle, promoting green design, cleaner production, and recycling. Through green processes and supplychain collaboration, it has achieved energy savings, carbon reduction, and efficient resource utilization, establishing a new benchmark for sustainable development in the pharmaceutical industry.

text: CSPC attaches great importance to identifying and managing environmental risks. text: 3.3 Resource Conservation

CSPC adheres to a green development philosophy and systematically promotes energy conservation, consumption reduction, and efficient resource utilization. By establishing an energy management system, building an intelligent energy management center, and increasing the proportion of green electricity used, the Group continues to optimize its energy structure. Meanwhile, it actively implements water-saving upgrades and recycling, and strengthens full-process control over packaging-material use, thereby improving resource efficiency and supporting the Company's green and low-carbon transformation.
3.3.1 Energy Management

CSPC has improved its energy management system, clarified responsibility allocation, and strengthened full-process control over energy use together with performance appraisal. By promoting energy conservation and consumption reduction and increasing the share of cleaner energy and resource efficiency, the Company continues to enhance energy-management effectiveness, with notable green-development results.
3.3.1.1 Energy Management System

In strict accordance with the Energy Conservation Law of the People's Republic of China , CSPC has formulated management systems such as the Energy Use Management System and the Operational Control Procedure for the Energy Management System. These systems cover energy-use management, energy-saving technological upgrades, energy statistics and analysis, energy targets and indicators, and energy metering, thereby standardizing production energy use.

Meanwhile, in line with international standards such as ISO 50001, we have established and improved an energy management mechanism covering the entire Group. In 2025, 7 subsidiaries had obtained ISO 50001 energy management system certification.
3.3.1.2 Energy Management Measures

In pursuit of its energy-saving and consumption-reduction goals, the subsidiaries of CSPC have actively advanced a range of energy-efficiency projects, covering process optimization, equipment upgrades, system retrofits, and energy recovery and reuse, thereby effectively reducing overall energy consumption.

Type of Measures | Specific Measures
Process Optimization | • Improvements to refined solution preparation equipment. Modification of the influent water supply mode for the micro-oxygen system. Optimization of purified-water system parameters. Recovery of residual heat from rectification for use in concentration processes.
Equipment Upgrades | • Replacement of pumps with energy-efficient models. Installation of thermo- compression distilled-water units to replace multi-effect distilled-water units. Replacement of coal-fired boilers with natural-gas boilers.
System Retrofits | • Interconnection retrofit of the compressed-air system. Addition of phase-change energy savers to the air-conditioning system. Economical operation of refrigeration systems. Combined operation of utility systems.

text: The Group has continued to drive the digital and intelligent transformation of energy management, significantly improving management efficiency. At present, we have established three intelligent energy management centers with data analysis and management capabilities, enabling the real-time collection and transmission of energy-use data. Key high-energy-consuming subsidiaries have now largely completed data integration.
Case Study: Automation Upgrade at the No.1 Manufacturing Center

In 2025, the No.1 Manufacturing Center carried out an automation upgrade of the utility system in Zone A. By installing automatic control modules, the center enabled automatic start-stop control, variable-frequency operation, and intelligent matching of equipment, allowing dynamic adjustment of energy supply and improved operating efficiency. Over the year, the project reduced electricity consumption by 900,000 kWh and saved RMB 594,000 in electricity costs, effectively advancing both green energy conservation and intelligent development.

text: Hazardous-waste transfers are carried out on a regular basis, with complete transfer manifests and full traceability throughout the process.

For non-hazardous waste, the Group actively promotes classified recycling and resource recovery. A full-process classified management system has been established for non-hazardous waste such as waste paper and discarded packaging materials, with standardized collection facilities and complete management records to ensure traceability and controllability. Through measures such as optimizing production processes, improving automation, and refining material-mixing ratios, the Group reduces scrap and defective products at the source. Meanwhile, it promotes green procurement and design, prioritizing recyclable and easy-to-recover raw materials and packaging materials to reduce resource waste.

In terms of circular utilization, the Group has established a closed-loop mechanism of "issue-recover-reuse"for packaging materials, promotes the unified collection of office and domestic waste, and entrusts professional institutions with resource recovery and treatment. In 2025, the compliant treatment rate for non-hazardous waste across the Group was 100%.

text: 3.4.2 Green Office

CSPC actively promotes the concept of green office operations and is committed to building a resource-efficient and environmentally friendly workplace. Through waste sorting, paperless office initiatives, and the implementation of energy-saving and water-saving measures, the Group effectively consumes fewer resources and generates less waste, thereby advancing the green transformation of office operations.

In addition, the Group continues to carry out green dining initiatives such as the "Clean Plate Campaign," enhancing employees' awareness of conservation and environmental responsibility. Through a combination of institutional guidance and culture-building, the Group is gradually fostering a green office culture in which all employees participate and practice sustainability together.
People-Oriented Growing Together

112 At a critical stage when the pharmaceutical industry is accelerating its transition toward innovation and internationalization, CSPC regards talent development as a core strategic investment. Upholding the talent philosophy of "valuing the capable, embracing diversity, and helping people achieve success," we are committed to building a sustainable talent management system that provides solid humancapital support for the Group's ongoing transformation and high-quality development.

text: Talent is the core driving force behind the Group's sustainable development and an important foundation for fulfilling our social responsibilities and creating diverse value. Through compliant employment practices and diversity policies, we attract outstanding talent broadly; through a competitive compensation and benefits system, we protect employee rights and interests; and through open communication channels, we promote organizational collaboration.

text: 4.1.1 Compliant Employment and Diversity

section: 4.1 Talent Attraction / Case Study: "Taima Business War" Simulation Training Promotes Diverse Communication and Exchange
text: CSPC has always regarded lawful employment and humane offboarding management as core elements of ESG governance. We publicly commit to complying with the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) and the core conventions of the International Labour Organization (ILO), and strictly observe national laws and regulations such as the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Special Provisions on Labor Protection for Female Employees. We have established systems including the Labor Relations Management System, Attendance and Leave Management System, Employee Separation Management System, Anti-Discrimination and Anti-Harassment Management Procedures, Anti-Forced Labor, Anti-Discrimination, Anti-Harassment and Anti-Abuse Management Procedures, and the Anti-Discrimination Management System. These form a full-lifecycle employment management framework supported by a digital human resources information system, safeguarding employees' lawful rights and interests at every stage from onboarding to departure. In 2025, the labor-contract signing rate, social-insurance coverage rate, and additional group accidental-insurance coverage rate for employees all reached 100%, and labor relations remained harmonious and stable.

section: 4.1 Talent Attraction / Case Study: "Taima Business War" Simulation Training Promotes Diverse Communication and Exchange
text: The Group and its subsidiaries firmly follow the spirit of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and regulations such as the Provisions on the Prohibition of Child Labor. We have established rules and procedures including the Child Labor and Underage Worker Protection Management Procedure, Regulations on the Prohibition of Child Labor, and the Procedure for Prohibiting Forced Labor, and categorically prohibit any form of child labor or forced labor. Specific measures are taken to prevent such incidents. During recruitment, we strictly verify candidates' basic information and age, and, with their authorization, conduct background checks to assess their eligibility for employment, ensuring the authenticity and validity of employee identities and preventing child labor and forced labor at the source. During the reporting period, there were no violations involving forced labor or child labor.

section: 4.1 Talent Attraction / Case Study: "Taima Business War" Simulation Training Promotes Diverse Communication and Exchange
text: The Group places great importance on internationally recognized labor and human-rights standards and actively accepts external assessments. We successfully passed the PSCI social responsibility audit, which reviewed our human-rights and labor practices, including labor protection, occupational health and safety, freedom of employment choice, non-discrimination, compensation and benefits, working hours, and working conditions. The final audit result was positive, with no major non-conformities.

section: 4.1 Talent Attraction / Case Study: "Taima Business War" Simulation Training Promotes Diverse Communication and Exchange
text: We firmly believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive team is a core driver of innovation and sustainable development. Accordingly, we have established the CSPC Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Policy. In talent recruitment and selection, we strictly follow the principle of non-discrimination and do not differentiate among candidates on the basis of education, religion, nationality, work background, marital status, gender, ethnicity, or race. During the initial résumé-screening stage, we also implement an anonymized screening mechanism that removes personal information such as ethnicity, ensuring that evaluation focuses on individual capability and potential. In internal promotion and compensation systems, we strictly prohibit any discrimination based on gender, age, or race. Diversity Target: By 2025, maintain a proportion of women in mid- to seniormanagement positions of no less than 40%.

text: To deepen the concept of diversity, we organized diversity-themed training across multiple organizational systems, aiming to break down professional silos and strengthen cross-department collaboration. For example, in the "Taima Business War"simulation training for senior managers, management personnel from R&D, production, marketing, and functional departments were mixed into teams to jointly address complex challenges involving market competition, product development, and operations management. Through scenario-based simulation, participants from different functions gained a deeper understanding of one another's responsibilities and needs, effectively enhancing mutual trust and collaborative efficiency, and laying a practical foundation for stronger overall organizational collaboration.

In addition, we actively attract graduates from ethnic minority groups through channels such as campus recruitment. In this way, we strive to build a diverse talent pool and foster an organizational culture characterized by equality, inclusion, and openness.

text: To strengthen the attraction and retention of young talent, the Group has implemented targeted incentive measures. We provide reserve talent and management trainees with special onboarding subsidies that are competitive within the industry, and actively assist them in connecting with local government talent-introduction policies such as talent green cards and housing subsidies. We continue to increase investment in the long-term development of talent and provide employees with comprehensive support from the start of their careers through long-term growth.

The Group values long-term development and benefit-sharing with core talent. Jiancheng Limited, the shareholder of the company, launched an equity incentive plan in 2022, covering more than 200 key employees in management, technology, and business roles, and completed the first phase of vesting in 2025. On January 23, 2026, the compamy announced that, under the plan, it had conditionally granted a total of 46,462,500 restricted shares free of charge to 727 selected employees of the group, subject to acceptance by the grantees and the fulfillment of certain vesting conditions and performance targets.Going forward, we plan to introduce a dedicated employee shareholding plan for outstanding younger employees with high potential, further building a talentdevelopment ecosystem characterized by innovation, growth, and sustainability.
Performance Improvement Feedback

While strengthening incentives for high-performing employees, high-potential employees, and employees in key positions, we also pay close attention to employees whose performance needs improvement and provide them with coaching and support. In this way, we promote a performance culture of continuous improvement and shared growth, realize coordinated enhancement of individual and organizational performance, and foster a virtuous cycle linking value creation with value distribution.
4.1.2.2 Benefits and Care

The Group strives to create a work environment in which employees feel secure, cared for, and a strong sense of belonging. We strictly comply with national and local laws and regulations to ensure that all employees enjoy comprehensive statutory leave benefits, including annual leave, marriage leave, maternity leave, childcare leave, and breastfeeding leave. We stipulate that before an employee's child reaches the age of three, all employees are entitled to childcare leave each year, with the number of leave days implemented in accordance with the policy in force for that year.

In addition, based on employees' multi-level needs, we have tailored a systematic and diversified set of dedicated benefits policies covering all types of positions across the Group. Through digital tools such as mobile application platforms, we continuously optimize the delivery, inquiry, and communication of benefits information, enabling employees to understand and enjoy various rights and benefits conveniently and promptly, and truly putting into practice the workplace philosophy of "live seriously, work happily."
Comprehensive Health Protection

In accordance with national and local requirements, employees are enrolled in the "five insurances and one housing fund," and additional group accidental injury insurance and traffic accident insurance are provided, creating a sound basic protection system.
Regular health checkups are organized for all employees, with attention to physical well-being and a focus on prevention, reflecting a long-term investment in employee health.
Major illness insurance and commercial insurance cover all employees.
Heating subsidies are provided during the heating season.

Facilities such as staff canteens, medical stations, gyms, and mother-and-baby rooms are available in office parks and are open to employees free of charge or at low cost, offering practical support for work and daily life.

The Group holds themed activities during major holidays-such as handicraft exhibitions and prize quizzes on International Women's Day-and distributes gifts or red envelopes. Birthday wishes and birthday red envelopes are also provided, enhancing employees' sense of happiness and cultural identity.

The Group issued the Guiding Opinions on the Development of CSPC Sports and Cultural Associations in 2025. Headquarters departments, business divisions, and subsidiaries actively responded by establishing a diverse range of sports and cultural clubs, including yoga, cycling, badminton, basketball, reading, and photography, thereby enhancing employee well-being and team cohesion.
As of December 2025, the number of sports and cultural associations had increased to 47, covering more than 2,200 employees.

text: We strictly follow the employee representative congress system and convene meetings on schedule each year to review the annual operating report and draft major policies that materially affect employees' interests. Resolutions are reviewed and voted on by employee representatives and then disclosed to all employees. To deepen democratic participation, the labor union regularly organizes the collection of employee proposals and coordinates the study, implementation, and feedback of those proposals with relevant departments to ensure that reasonable employee concerns receive effective responses. In addition, the labor union has established a labor dispute mediation committee to provide employees with a formal consultation and mediation channel and further protect their labor rights.
4.1.3.3 Consultation and Complaints

We have established and maintain a formal, strictly confidential human resources grievance and reporting procedure. Any complaint involving discrimination, harassment, violations of fairness and justice, or other improper conduct is handled through a formal process that triggers a timely, thorough, and impartial investigation, while ensuring the strict confidentiality of complainant information. Relevant handling departments and managers are required to perform their duties objectively and are accountable for the investigation outcomes. We prohibit retaliation in any form, and any substantiated retaliatory behavior is dealt with seriously to safeguard workplace fairness and employees' legitimate rights and interests. In addition, we have built an intelligent Q&A platform that allows employees to obtain information efficiently through self-service inquiries, thereby improving internal communication efficiency.
Table: Formal Process for Handling Employee Inquiries, Complaints, and Feedback

Employee | • Employees submit inquiries or complaint feedback through the "I Want to Consult" module in the shared services portal. • For inquiries, employees may consult online by selecting a question category and a specific question, or they may transfer to manual input and enter the question directly. • For complaints and feedback, employees select the feedback type and enter the specific issue.
Function/ Segment Leaders | • When the system receives an employee inquiry, it automatically assigns a responder, who must respond and address the issue within two days. • When the system receives an employee complaint or feedback submission, the operations lead handles it based on the reported content. • Depending on the type and substance of the complaint, cases are divided into two categories: direct resolution and coordinated resolution. • For directly resolvable matters, the relevant responsible person may be assigned to reply. For matters requiring coordination, the next step is to contact the HR function of the employee's company for coordinated resolution.

text: Employee Self-Service Q&A

To build an efficient and transparent internal communication mechanism, we officially launched the "Employee Self-Service Q&A" module in the EHR system, using digital tools to create an intelligent platform that integrates knowledge-base management, inquiry handling, and feedback follow-up. The platform enables 100% closed-loop resolution of employee inquiries. Based on high-frequency inquiry needs, we sorted and built 41 standard FAQ entries, established a keyword-based automatic matching and instant response mechanism, and improved inquiry handling efficiency. For issues not already covered, the system automatically routes the case to the appropriate responsible person based on the employee's business unit, ensuring precise assignment and timely response. In 2025, the platform handled 64 employee inquiries, all of which received effective feedback and resolution. We also review inquiry data regularly, synchronize high-frequency issues into the knowledge base, and continuously optimize service content to help employees obtain information efficiently and create a smoother, more convenient internal communication environment.
4.2 Talent Development

To achieve the Company's long-term strategic objectives, we uphold a forward-looking human resources philosophy and focus on internal talent cultivation, assessment, and development-oriented training, providing a steady stream of endogenous momentum for the organization's sustainable development.
4.2.1 Formal Talent Pipeline Development Strategy

To ensure the sustained development of the Group's business and preserve its innovative vitality, we conduct early-stage position assessments and talent research, clarify role requirements, establish talent reserve and development plans for different business types, accurately identify high-potential talent, expand the pipeline for key positions, and strengthen succession preparation.

We have built a comprehensive and diversified recruitment system that broadly attracts outstanding talent aligned with our corporate culture and development needs. Our main recruitment channels are as follows:

text: At a critical stage when the pharmaceutical industry is accelerating its transformation toward innovation and internationalization, we regards talent development as a core strategic investment. We have established a training management system featuring unified Group-level planning and detailed implementation by subsidiaries. At the Group level, the Training Department under the Organizational Talent Development Department coordinates overall training planning and resource management, while each subsidiary appoints part-time learning coordinators responsible for supporting Group initiatives and advancing internal training implementation.

section: 4.2.2 Talent Training and Empowerment / Employee Training System
text: At the Group level, we have formulated and continuously improved a series of systems, including the Training Management System, clarifying the respective training responsibilities of the Group and its subsidiaries and standardizing training plan development, project execution, platform operation and maintenance, and examination procedures. This ensures that training work remains aligned with the Group's strategic direction and operates in a standardized and well-regulated manner. On this basis, each subsidiary further refines implementation rules in light of its actual business conditions.

section: 4.2.2 Talent Training and Empowerment / Employee Training System
text: In 2025, our training work remained tightly aligned with the Group's strategic objectives and focused on industry challenges. We initially established a tiered, progressive, full-lifecycle training framework covering new employee onboarding, on-the-job capability enhancement, management development, and reserve-cadre development, with the goal of cultivating highly qualified talent with innovative spirit, professional competence, and an international outlook.

text: For mid-level managers in R&D, production, and functional systems, we designed advanced training covering topics such as situational leadership and building high-performance teams, enhancing managers' ability to coach employees, motivate teams, and drive performance.
Employee Training System
· Front-Line Managers

Front-line managers are the core force for executing strategy and leading teams. We provide targeted empowerment for newly promoted managers to help them quickly adapt to their new roles, while also going deep into key business regions to standardize management practices and strengthen practical coaching skills.

For newly promoted front-line managers in R&D, production, marketing, and functional systems, we delivered training on Role Transition and Employee Coaching to support their managerial transition. For the marketing system, we also offered Regional Planning training to strengthen sales management capability and accelerate professional product promotion.

To address the fact that first- and second-line managers in the marketing system still rely heavily on experience and need more systematic capability in team management and business coaching, we launched targeted management capability reinforcement training focused on key regions and key positions. Professional trainers were sent into the field to provide on-site instruction and one-toone coaching, helping managers systematically master standardized management methods and practical business guidance skills, promoting the standardization of management behavior, the practical conversion of skills, and the sustained improvement of overall team performance.
Employee Training System
· Potential Reserve Talent

To respond to intensifying industry competition and upgraded talent needs, we launched dedicated training for high-potential and reserve talent to strengthen professional capability and overall quality, build a high-quality talent pipeline, and reserve future leadership for the Company's long-term development.

Outstanding mid-level managers from R&D, production, marketing, and functional systems are selected as executive reserve talent for systematic development. In the first stage, structured-thinking tools are introduced to help participants establish a comprehensive and innovative thinking framework. The second stage focuses on team leadership development and strengthens the ability to improve team performance in diverse environments. This stage also emphasizes strategic vision and whole-picture thinking, laying a solid foundation for future promotion and development.

High-potential employees in the production system are selected for training. The program is supported by a strong faculty, including well-known professors from Hebei Medical University, Hebei University of Science and Technology, and other institutions, as well as seasoned experts from regulatory authorities who provide practical guidance. Participants systematically study advanced production processes, quality management methods, and relevant regulatory and compliance requirements, and then apply what they learn to optimize production processes and quality control, effectively improving production efficiency and product quality and further strengthening the Group's core competitiveness in manufacturing.
Employee Training System
· Front-Line Employees

To match the capability requirements of positions across R&D, production, marketing, and other professional systems, we actively organize skills enhancement training for front-line employees. The training combines general knowledge, professional theory, and practical job skills to improve technical capability and overall work effectiveness.
· R&D
focuses on standard laboratory operations, data management, end-to-end project control, and relevant regulations and policies.
· Production
combines classroom teaching, drills, and competitions to effectively implement legal and regulatory requirements and management concepts related to quality, safety, production, and equipment.
Marketing
while strengthening product knowledge and regional management skills, it also emphasizes on-site joint visits and coaching to promote real-world application of what employees learn.
· New Employee Training

To help new employees quickly integrate into our culture and meet job requirements, we use diversified training formats and targeted course design to promote capability development and cultural alignment, laying a solid talent foundation for the Group's high-quality development.
Campus Reserve Trainee Onboarding Training

For new members of the 2025 Shiyao Camp cohort, we designed a dedicated onboarding training program centered on cultural integration and career growth. Through four modules, namely Team Building and Icebreaking, Role Transition and Cultural Integration, Exploring CSPC and Pursuing Excellence, and Shared Brilliance, Co-Creating the Future, the program supports cultural integration and professional transition.
· Social Recruitment Onboarding Training

For newly hired employees with prior work experience, the Group organizes system-specific online and offline training tailored to the business needs of R&D, production, marketing, and other systems, helping new hires quickly adapt to the new environment, meet role requirements, and effectively connect their professional experience with the Group's business needs.
Employee Training System
· Continuous Learning for All Employees

To enhance professional competence and overall capability across the workforce and build a learning organization, we launched a series of continuous learning initiatives for all employees, stimulating learning enthusiasm and initiative while strengthening both professional capability and overall quality.
Xuanxing Learning Management Initiative: Tiered Learning and Precise Empowerment
Built on an online platform, the initiative pushes learning content by employee level and job requirements:
Senior management: strategic and industry-trend reading to support macro-level decision-making.
Mid-level management: greater focus on team management and project execution.
Grassroots employees: emphasis on job skills and deeper professional knowledge.

This precise tiering improves learning relevance and effectiveness, while progress-tracking functions support both self-directed learning and organizational supervision, ensuring that training objectives are achieved and driving stepwise capability growth across the workforce.

We support employees in continuous learning and on-the-job advancement, promoting the enhancement of their professional capabilities, and encourage them to obtain official certifications such as professional degrees and certificates. In 2025, four senior executives successfully graduated from the MBA program at CEIBS. In addition, the Group actively organized and supported all employees in participating in professional technical title appraisal, with a total of 282 employees successfully passing the evaluation. Among them, 84 received senior professional titles and now play a leading role in technical R&D and management; 132 received intermediate professional titles and serve as the backbone across business fields; and 66 received junior professional titles, bringing fresh vitality to their teams. Professional title evaluation not only provides authoritative recognition of employees' expertise, but also effectively inspires continuous learning and professional improvement across the workforce, accumulating deep talent capital for the organization.

section: Case Study: Enterprise New Apprenticeship Training For the Development of Skilled Talent
text: To implement national requirements for building the industrial workforce, we systematically carried out the enterprise new apprenticeship training program. The program adopts a school-enterprise cooperation model combining work and study, with the aim of improving the professional quality and practical capabilities of skilled talent and strengthening the talent foundation for the Group's sustainable development. In 2025, CSPC organized a total of 1,352 newly hired and transferred frontline production employees in skilled roles from multiple subsidiaries, including Ouyi, Zhongnuo, CSPC NBP, CSPC Innovation, and CSPC Shengxue, to participate in the program. Using a deeply integrated 'theory plus practice' model, the program provided 160 class hours of theoretical learning and 240 class hours of on-the-job practical training, effectively improving participants' theoretical knowledge and vocational skills. After the program, 1,071 participants passed vocational skill level assessments and obtained national vocational skill certificates such as Senior Pharmaceutical Preparation Worker, Pharmaceutical Preparation Technician, and Senior Organic Synthesis Worker.

Safety Risk Management

The Group organized its subsidiaries to continue carrying out risk identification activities and identified a total of 23,609 risks, including 17 major risks and 51 relatively significant risks. We classify all risks according to severity, formulate targeted control measures, establish regular review and inspection mechanisms, and implement closedloop risk management.
Emergency Response Drills

The Group continued strengthening its emergency response capabilities by organizing emergency drills. We have established a four-tier emergency management system and regularly conduct comprehensive drills, specialized drills, and firefighting drills, effectively improving all employees' risk response and emergency disposal capabilities and preventing or mitigating the impact of accidents.
Safety Management of Business Partners and Contractors

Through dedicated policies such as the Measures for the Safety Management of Related Parties and External Workers and the Safety Management Procedures for Outsourced Construction, we have established a full-process management system covering admission, operations, and evaluation. This system clearly defines qualification review requirements, safety training, process supervision, and evaluation standards for related parties, extending the Company's safety requirements to every stage of the value chain and ensuring that on-site risks remain under control.

text: 4.3.2 Occupational Health Management

In accordance with laws and regulations including the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases, the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Employers'Occupational Health Monitoring, the Technical Specifications for Occupational Health Monitoring, the Provisions on Occupational Health Management in Workplaces, and the Measures for the Reporting of Occupational Hazard Projects , the Group requires all member companies to comply with applicable occupational health requirements in their places of operation and to formulate and implement the Occupational Health Management System and the Occupational Health Examination and Testing Plan, with regular monitoring of occupational hazard factors in the workplace.

We have fully integrated occupational health and safety management into the core of our production and operations, and have defined the "Five Zeros and One Low" occupational health and safety management targets.

section: CSPC Occupational Health and Safety Management Targets / 4.3.3 Building a Safety Culture
text: In strict accordance with the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and the Administrative Provisions on Safety Training for Production and Business Operation Entities, the Group has established and continuously improved the EHS Education and Training Management System and formulated and implemented an annual EHS Training Plan. Through a model that combines online learning, offline practical training, and position-specific drills, we provide comprehensive coverage of both fundamental safety knowledge and advanced professional skills. Leveraging the "Xuanxing" training platform, we provide online courses and video training and organize in-person training sessions, workplace safety knowledge competitions, and thematic lectures for safety personnel, thereby enhancing employees' safety awareness and emergency response capabilities. In addition, during Fire Safety Month, we organize company-wide emergency evacuation drills and conduct multiple on-site emergency response drills in critical areas such as confined spaces, hazardous chemicals, electric shock, mechanical injury, and special equipment, strengthening practical emergency response capabilities and reinforcing the foundation for safe production.

text: In January 2026, CSPC and AstraZeneca signed a strategic R&D cooperation and licensing agreement for innovative long-acting peptide drugs. Relying on the Group's proprietary sustained-release delivery platform and peptide medicine discovery platform, the two parties will jointly advance the development of eight long-acting weight management and innovation projects including SYH2082. The Group will grant AstraZeneca exclusive global rights outside Greater China and has the right to receive an upfront payment of USD 1.2 billion, with total milestone payments of up to USD 17.3 billion plus double-digit sales royalties. This cooperation not only set a new industry record for overseas expansion, but also strongly validated the power of the Group's innovative technology platforms in driving its globalization strategy.

text: As of the end of 2025, the number of specifications of products on sale had continued to grow, with extensive coverage across all 31 provinces and municipalities in China. Generic Medicine Sales | • The Group markets a variety of products in low- and middle-income countries to enhance patient access to medicines, including Amoxicillin Capsules, Ceftriaxone Sodium for Injection, Ampicillin Capsules, Procaine Benzylpenicillin Fortified Sodium for Injection, Benzylpenicillin Sodium for Injection, Meropenem for Injection, and Azithromycin Film-Coated Tablets.
Pharmaco- vigilance System Development | • The Group has established a comprehensive monitoring and reporting mechanism for adverse drug reactions (ADRs) overseas. When adverse reactions occur outside China, the Group collaborates with local agents and customers to report to the local regulatory authorities in accordance with local regulations, and simultaneously notifies other customers marketing the same batch of products to submit reports. For serious adverse reactions occurring overseas, the Group ensures reporting to the National Center for Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring within 15 days upon notification. If a drug is suspended from sale, use, or withdrawn from the market overseas due to adverse reactions, a written report will be submitted to the National Medical Products Administration and the National Center for Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring within 24 hours. All other adverse reaction information is incorporated into the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) system for medicines.
Medical Personnel Training | • The Group actively dispatches personnel to provide guidance to local medical staff, and regularly organizes experts to conduct on-site exchanges and training to continuously strengthen the local medication safety system. In 2025, the Group organized 9 exchanges between hospitals in China and Southeast Asian countries, introducing the advantages and administration methods of TNK to overseas physicians, and disseminating product information on NBP and TNK to experts in Southeast Asian countries.

section: 5.2.3 Rare Disease Drug R&D and Investment
text: CSPC has been deeply engaged in the field of rare diseases (orphan drugs) and is committed to improving the current shortage of clinical treatment options for rare diseases. Through independent R&D and technological innovation, the Group now has nine products that have obtained orphan drug designation from the U.S. FDA. For marketed products, Narusobimab Injection and Nintedanib Ethanesulfonate Soft Capsules have been successfully approved for marketing, effectively filling treatment gaps in the relevant fields.

section: 5.2.3 Rare Disease Drug R&D and Investment
text: In 2025, the Group continued to increase R&D investment and focused on rare malignant tumors, autoimmune diseases, and metabolic disorders. A total of 11 products in development made major progress during the clinical development stage. We not only focus on clinical value, but also improve ease of use through technological enhancement and are committed to developing high-value biosimilars to reduce the financial burden on patients.

text: 5.3 Social Welfare

CSPC actively fulfills its corporate social responsibility, focusing on industrial assistance and educational support, participating deeply in rural revitalization, and continuously carrying out public welfare projects in areas such as education support and healthcare. In 2025, the Group's total charitable donations amounted to RMB 61.5464 million, benefiting 105,880 person-times, with 95,469 service hours devoted to public welfare.

In 2015, CSPC initiated the establishment of the Hebei CSPC Puen Charity Foundation, focusing on livelihoodrelated areas such as poverty relief, elderly care, support for the sick, and education assistance. The Foundation was rated a 5A social organization in both 2019 and 2024, and during the reporting period it was also awarded the title of "National Advanced Social Organization."
5.3.1 Rural Revitalization

CSPC actively supports the rural revitalization strategy. Leveraging its pharmaceutical expertise, it focuses on building healthy rural communities, improving primary healthcare capacity, cultivating local health talent, and promoting the sustainable development of medicinal resources, thereby effectively safeguarding farmers' health and fulfilling corporate social responsibility. In 2025, the "Light Spring Rain" rural revitalization support project donated RMB 1.9526 million, with volunteer service totaling 160 hours.

text: Case Study: CSPC Rushes Emergency Medicine Donations to Flood-hit Chengde, Hebei

section: 5.3.3 Earthquake Relief and Disaster Response / 5.3.2 Educational Support
text: In July 2025, Chengde City in Hebei Province experienced rare torrential rainfall that triggered severe flooding. In some areas, transport links were cut off, homes were damaged, and daily life was seriously affected. CSPC responded quickly, contacted relevant Chengde authorities to learn what supplies were urgently needed, and extended assistance to affected residents by donating urgently needed medicines ( 4,000 boxes of amoxicillin capsules and 4,000 boxes of ibuprofen granules), thereby putting into practice the social responsibility of a pharmaceutical enterprise.

section: 5.3.3 Earthquake Relief and Disaster Response / 5.3.2 Educational Support
text: On 26 November, a sudden fire broke out at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, New Territories, Hong Kong, causing significant casualties and drawing widespread concern across the country. CSPC immediately launched an emergency relief plan, actively coordinated with relevant government authorities, and donated HKD 10 million in cash and medicines to support the urgent resettlement of affected residents and their basic living needs during the transitional period. CSPC will continue to monitor disaster relief and rescue efforts, and is willing to work hand in hand with all sectors of society to mobilize resources for emergency assistance and post-disaster reconstruction, helping those affected overcome this difficult time as soon as possible.

text: As a core platform through which CSPC implements the Healthy China strategy, the CSPC Puen Charity Foundation has long participated in charitable medical assistance for severe and major diseases. Through programs such as the Assistance for Tumor Patients in Difficult Circumstances, the Medical Assistance for Patients in Difficult Circumstances, and the Patient Assistance Program for patients from minimum-living-guarantee households, extremely poor households, low-income families, and families pushed into poverty by illness, the Foundation further advances the Healthy China development strategy. In these areas of major disease medical assistance, the Group donated 235,000 boxes of medicines and assisted 104,590 person-times.

text: Launched in 2022, the "Assistance for Tumor Patients in Difficult Circumstances" program aims to reduce the medical burden on severely ill patients from low-income and other disadvantaged households through direct financial assistance, thereby providing meaningful support to more families facing hardship caused by serious illness. In 2025, the program entered five prefecture-level cities in three provinces and carried out 75 patient support and care activities. Program expenditures reached RMB 3.605 million , benefiting 468 disadvantaged patients from minimum-living-guarantee and similar households, with volunteer service totaling 8,988 hours.

text: Congenital heart diseases such as atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus, and pulmonary artery stenosis, as well as acquired heart diseases such as coronary heart disease, hypertensive heart disease, and rheumatic heart disease, pose severe challenges for many families in difficult circumstances. To alleviate this hardship, the Group officially launched the "Medical Assistance for Patients in Difficult Circumstances" program in 2024, aiming to sustain life and restore hope to every heart awaiting treatment. In 2025, the program spent RMB 947,200 , organized 30 patient support and care activities, assisted 90 patients in difficult circumstances, and contributed 1,290 volunteer service hours.
